articleTitle: A Novel Method for Determining the Source of the Second Traveling Wave in Fault Location of VSC-HVDC Lines
abstract: The traveling wave-based fault location methods for VSC-HVDC lines typically require detecting the second traveling wave after faults occur. However, the second traveling wave may come from different reflected traveling waves, leading to different ways of calculating the fault distance. Therefore, it is necessary to determine the source of the second traveling wave, which is one of the difficulties. This paper analyzes the characteristics of the second voltage traveling wave from different sources and proposes a novel determination method. It uses the sign of the voltage change rate at the arrival time of the second traveling wave front to determine its source and is applicable to both sin-gle-line-to-ground faults and line-to-line faults. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified in PSCAD/EMTDC. The simulation results demonstrate that this method can accurately determine the source of the second traveling wave under various fault conditions.

articleTitle: Study on AC Breakdown Characteristics of Gas-Liquid Two-Phase Fluorocarbon in Phase Change Cooling Transformer
abstract: When the transformer uses fluorocarbon compounds for phase change cooling, bubbles will be generated in the gas-liquid two-phase medium, threatening the safe and reliable operation of the transformer. The discharging breakdown characteristics of gas-liquid two-phase dielectrics are closely related to the generation and aggregation of thermally induced bubbles. In this paper, a set of experimental equipment for measuring the breakdown voltage of gas-liquid two-phase dielectrics is designed and the related experiment is carried out. In this experiment, the experimental curve of dielectric breakdown voltage versus heat flux density is obtained. In addition, design recommendations for insulation margin of gas-liquid two-phase media in high-field-strength equipment applications are proposed to enhance reliability and performance.

articleTitle: A design of common mode EMI filter for on board high power equipment of train traction system
abstract: As one of the typical interference sources, highpower equipment in train traction system will produce certain electromagnetic interference to signal equipment and other weak current systems. Therefore, it is of great significance to carry out research on common mode interference suppression technology of on-board high-power equipment of train traction system, to study a filter device which can be used to suppress common mode interference of high-power equipment in train and vehicle system, reduce electromagnetic interference caused by train traction system, and solve electromagnetic interference problems in actual vehicle operation process. Aiming at the serious electromagnetic conducted interference caused by the output of train traction system to traction motor, this paper analyzes the characteristics of common mode noise generated by traction system and the requirements of EMC national standards. Based on the theoretical basis of design of EMI passive common mode filter and the actual power level required, the frequency band and insertion loss of the filter are analyzed,According to two common mode inductors in traditional passive EMI filter, a three-dimensional structure is studied, and a common mode EMI filter which can be used in high-power equipment of train traction system is designed.

articleTitle: Research on the Virtual Inertia Integrated Control Strategy Based on Doubly-Fed Wind Turbine
abstract: With the large-scale wind power access to the power system, the capacity of conventional units and the proportion of output continues to decrease, while the increasing penetration of wind power caused by the decline in the system moment of inertia and frequency instability problems increased significantly, this paper establishes a dynamic response model of the frequency of the power system containing wind power, analyzes the virtual inertia of the wind turbine on the basis of the integrated control of the frequency, and proposes a new type of virtual inertia based on the regulating function integrated control strategy. control strategy, through the use of wind turbine rotor kinetic energy, effectively increase the system moment of inertia, through simulation to verify the effectiveness of the control strategy and improve the power system frequency response capability.

Author Keywords: the two areas with four generators

articleTitle: Low Voltage Ride Through Strategy for Islanded Wind-Solar Power Stations Based on Virtual Synchronous Generator
abstract: This study focuses on enhancing the stability of islanded wind-solar power stations under low-voltage fault conditions. These stations, integrating wind and solar energy, are connected to the grid via power electronic converters but face challenges related to the lack of inertia and damping in traditional control strategies. To address this issue, a low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) strategy based on the Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) is proposed, ensuring stable operation during grid low-voltage events. Theoretical analysis and simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy significantly improves the stability and reliability of islanded wind-solar power stations under low-voltage fault conditions.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Influence of Cable Coupling on the Distribution Ratio of Rail Transit Backflow under AC Power Supply System*
abstract: With the development of AC power supply system in rail transit, it has been found in actual operation that poor traction return channels can cause power frequency and harmonic interference in track circuits, damage to track insulation, and pose a threat to train safety. Among them, the electromagnetic coupling generated by cables in the electric traction environment can affect the traction return of trains, resulting in poor return flow. At present, there is limited research on the impact of return cable coupling on the return distribution of rail transit under AC power supply system, therefore it is necessary to study it. This article takes the actual parameters of a subway project in Guangzhou as a template, uses EMTP simulation software to establish a two-layer subway tunnel model, and studies its impact on the traction return system of rail transit under AC mode by changing the parameters of the return system. Research has found that changing the reflux system parameters before the equalization point has little effect on the reflux distribution ratio; The spatial distance between the return cable and the power supply cable within 2 meters has a significant impact on the return distribution ratio, but it is not related to the contact points of the return cable at the station or the number of return cables. The distribution of current shows a skin effect.

articleTitle: An Extended Droop Control Strategy Based on Virtual Impedance Matching for MEA Power Supply System with Pulsed Loads
abstract: The DC power supply system of more electric aircraft (MEA) has the inherent characteristics of low inertia and small capacity, make it easy to be impacted by the pulsed power loads (PPLs). Aiming at the stability of bus voltage under different flight phases, an extended droop control strategy based on virtual impedance matching is proposed for fuel cell/battery/supercapacitor hybrid power supply system of MEA. In the proposed method, the virtual inductor, virtual resistor and virtual capacitor droop control are adopted for fuel cell, battery and supercapacitor respectively, enabling the load power to be automatically divided into high-frequency, intermediate-frequency and low-frequency parts. Thus, the power demand could be compensated by each power supply units respectively, according to their output characteristics. The simulation results verify the correctness and validity of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Application of second-order generalized integral PLL method when inverter connecting with grid under harmonic background
abstract: In case of large number of distributed generation (DG) connected to grid, harmonic pollution becomes more seriously. DGs and grid-connected inverters are expected to participate in grid operation and management responsibly. Especially when the grid meets serious harmonic pollution, inverter’s grid connecting manipulation requires very high-precision phase angle detection. In these years, as a novel phase locked loop (PLL) method, second-order generalized integral (SOGI) PLL attracts more and more attentions. For inverter grid connecting manipulation purpose, in this paper, relationship between SOGI controller parameters and its dynamic performance are analyzed firstly. Then via SOGI, positive sequence components are extracted accurately and rapidly from the seriously polluted grid voltage. Using this information, inverter grid connecting controller can be designed. Through Matlab/Simulink simulation tool, above proposed method is justified and simulation results show its effectiveness when inverter connecting with grid under serious harmonic pollution.

articleTitle: A Study of Detecting the State of Grounding Conductor by Spectrum Analysis
abstract: Grounding system is an important part to protect the stable operation of power system and equipment safety. In the existing fault diagnosis and status assessment methods of grounding conductor, stoppage, power off or manual digging are often used. This paper presents a method of grounding conductor state detection based on spectrum analysis, which can detect the ground conductor state through the spectrum characteristics of ground impedance. Firstly, the simulation magnitudels of four common grounding conductors are established, and the phase-frequency and amplitude-frequency curves of grounding impedances of different grounding conductor structures are calculated. Secondly, the spectral response curves of grounding conductor length, equivalent radius and soil resistivity to impedance magnitude and impedance Angle of grounding impedance are analyzed. In this paper, it is found that the frequency response characteristic of ground impedance is feasible to detect the state of the grounding conductor.

articleTitle: Transient DC Bias Suppression Strategy for Dual Active Bridge DC/DC Converters Based on Adaptive Virtual Resistance Compensation
abstract: For dual active bridge (DAB) DC/DC converters, DC bias of the inductor current caused by the system parameters variation increases system losses, leads to core saturation, and even jeopardizes the safe and reliable operation. To solve it, a transient DC bias suppression strategy based on adaptive virtual resistance compensation is proposed in this paper. The transient mathematical model of a DAB converter with DC bias is built. On this basis, the phase shift is compensated to simulate the transient characteristic of real-resistance compensation, where the virtual resistance can be dynamically adjusted according to the DC bias. Thus, the transient DC bias can be suppressed without additional circuits, and the simulation results verify its feasibility and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Parameter Design of LLCL Filter for NPC Grid-Connected Inverter
abstract: This paper introduces a design method for LLCL filter of NPC grid-connected inverter. By analyzing the ripple current of NPC inverter in different switching states, the inverter side inductance, series capacitor and grid connected side inductance are designed by the side ripple ratio of the inverter, the branch series inductance is designed by the resonance at the switching frequency, the passive damping method is adopted to eliminate the resonance peak, and the branch resistance is designed. The parameters of each device of the designed LLCL filter meet the requirements of grid connection. The performance of LLCL filter is tested by MATLAB/Simulink simulation to achieve the purpose of grid connection.

articleTitle: Enhanced Diagnosis of the Broken Bar Fault in Induction Motors Through the Wiener Filter
abstract: For better diagnosis of the broken bar fault (BBF) of the induction motor, the performance of the Wiener filter (WF) for suppressing the fundamental frequency component (FFC) of the stator current signal (SCS) is explored through simulation and experiments. The WF utilizes the FFC of the supply voltage signal (SVS) to estimate the FFC of the SCS. Due to orthogonality of sinusoidal signals, the estimate of the FFC of the SCS contains little information of the sideband harmonics (SBHs). Then, subtracting the estimate of the FFC from the SCS suppresses the FFC significantly, with little impact on the SBHs, especially their amplitudes, which is validated by simulation. Thus, as revealed by the experimental results, the SBHs with their amplitudes can be unambiguously identified from the spectrum of the SCS processed by the WF, leading to feasibility of diagnosis of the BBF at its incipient stage through monitoring the amplitudes of the SBHs. Comparison of the performance of FFC suppression of the WF with that of the Kalman filter further illustrates superiority of the WF for FFC suppression. Therefore, our research demonstrates the aforementioned WF is pretty effective in the situation where diagnosis of induction motor faults through motor current signature analysis is hampered by the widened peak of the FFC of the SCS due to spectral leakage, especially in the case of the BBF.

articleTitle: Error Analysis of Current Transformer with Combined Magnetic Core under the Influence of DC Component
abstract: The increasing DC current component in the power supply system will have a great impact on the measurement accuracy of traditional current transformers. Since the hysteresis loop of the magnetic core material is nonlinear, the secondary current will be distorted when the measured current contains a DC component. In this paper, the distortion characteristics of the secondary current under different magnitudes of DC component and AC current are studied, and the hysteresis loop of the magnetic core material is considered. Then, the core structure of the transformer, which can accurately measure the current with the DC component, is studied. Specifically, high permeability permalloy and high saturation magnetic induction cold rolled silicon steel are combined radially, axially, and circumferentially. The analysis found that when the two types of materials are radially combined, and the inner layer is permalloy and the outer layer is cold-rolled silicon steel, the measurement accuracy is higher. The current transformer with combined magnetic core can not only reduce the measurement error of low excitation and no DC component, but also solve the problem of core saturation caused by DC component.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Negative Sequence Current-based and Current Residual-based Online Diagnosis Method for Inter-turn Faults in PMSM Drives
abstract: When the inter-turn faults (ITF) occur, the motor short-circuit current increases sharply, affecting the balance of the motor system, prolonged operation under this condition can cause irreversible damage to the entire motor system. Therefore, early diagnosis of ITF is critical to ensuring the reliability of the motor system. This article focuses on two kinds of fault diagnosis methods based on signal processing and analytical model, it compares and analyzes two kinds of fault diagnosis strategies based on negative sequence current and current residual, respectly. Initially, mathematical models representing both the healthy and fault states of the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) are established in a synchronous rotating reference frame. Then, the second-order generalized integrator (SOGI) is utilized to extract the negative sequence components in real-time, while current residual is obtained through an observer. Based on theses, corresponding fault detection indicators are proposed. Finally, a fault test platform is constructed to evaluate and compare the performance of the two diagnostic methods in terms of fault detection accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration of Integrated Energy Systems Based on Improved Genetic Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents an optimization method for integrated energy systems based on a genetic algorithm, aimed at achieving efficient energy management through multi-energy complementation, improving energy utilization efficiency, reducing carbon emissions, and optimizing economic performance. The study first constructs a capacity optimization model for the integrated energy system based on the resource conditions and energy demand of an industrial park, with the objective of minimizing total system costs and considering carbon trading costs. The system configuration was solved using a genetic algorithm, and simulations were conducted using actual load data from typical summer and winter days. The results show that the optimized system achieved renewable energy utilization rates of 93.59% and 90.0% in summer and winter, respectively, with carbon emissions reduced by approximately 20.46 tons and 17.25 tons. This research provides theoretical support for the design and control of integrated energy systems in industrial parks, demonstrating significant potential in energy conservation and emission reduction.

articleTitle: To Explore the Influence of Different Factors on The Potential Distribution of AC Power Subway Rails
abstract: With the rapid development of urban rail transit, AC power supply subway has gradually appeared in the public eye, and its rail potential distribution has attracted attention from all walks of life. In this paper, a CDEGS simulation model is built for a subway line in Guangzhou, and the distribution of rail potential under a single train station, a single train double station and a double train single station is simulated. When the end of the section where the train is located is disconnected, the voltage value of copper-clad steel and flat steel will increase dramatically; The operation of multiple trains in different sections is similar to that of a single train.

articleTitle: Analysis of an Accident Caused by Excitation Inrush Current Leading to Wide-Band Harmonic Monitoring Protection Action
abstract: A technical analysis of a misoperation accident of converter station caused by excitation surge current leads to misoperation of broadband harmonic monitoring and protection. Through the collection of measured data at the accident site, the specific process of the excitation surge current triggering misoperation is analyzed, and the reasons for the protection action are given. The working principle and misoperation mechanism of broadband harmonic monitoring and protection were modeled and simulated, and the laboratory reproduction of the accident process was carried out. On this basis, this paper puts forward technical measures and suggestions to prevent the recurrence of similar accidents.

articleTitle: Optimization and Adjustment Method of Intra-Day Tie Line Schedule in Bulk Bilateral Transaction Market Environment
abstract: The formulation of tie line schedule is a heavy workload and complex process in bulk bilateral transaction market environment, while the existing artificial establishment mode for large power system will not be able to accommodate the subsequent grid-provincial coordination plan. For this reason, a linked list model of electricity trade and tie line schedule and a tree cluster model of large trans-regional power source and tie line are proposed according to the actual situation of the North China power grid. Based on the former model, a plan making optimization model is proposed with minimum transmission costs as the optimization objective and the contract power quantity, transmission limit of tie line as constraints. The optimization model is solved with ergodic theory based breadth-first search and cyclic iteration. The model contains a complete description of various problems of the tie line schedule in the North China power grid, realizing automatic and efficient adjustment of the schedule. Actual operation results show that the proposed model is valid and effective, while simulation results exhibit the unique technical advantage of the model for tie line schedule adjustment in bulk bilateral transaction market environment.

articleTitle: Research on Platform Construction of MMC-HVDC Digital Analog Hybrid Simulation Based on ADPSS
abstract: With the development of new energy, it poses a huge challenge to safe and stable operation of the electrical power systems. The transmission technology based on modular multilevel converter (MMC) solves the problems connecting with weak AC systems. When conducting real-time simulation of large-scale ACDC power grids containing MMC-HVDC, the number of nodes is huge, which makes the simulation process extremely slow. The Thevenin equivalent modeling method is used to simulate the electromagnetic transient simulation method of the converter valve. This paper presents a platform based on advanced digital power system simulator (ADPSS). Referring to the parameters of Yu to E ± 420kV back-to-back MMC-HVDC transmission project, the accuracy of the constructed model is verified through comparing result with the actual project. The simulation platform proposed in the article can be used to simulate the large-scale AC/DC interconnection power grid accurately.

articleTitle: High Energy Density Li-ion Battery by Ultra-thick Dry Coating Cathode
abstract: In the pursuit of a sustainable future, lithium-ion battery is an indispensable energy storage device in grid-scale energy storage systems. However, the prevalent cathode electrode manufacturing processes encounter obstacles in terms of their environmental harmfulness and costliness, primarily attributed to the toxic solvent desiccation and reclamation stages. Moreover, the reliance on lithium-ion batteries particularly underscores the necessity for augmenting energy density, both in terms of volume and weight, with the cathode as the pivotal factor. Dry electrode fabrication emerges as an economical approach to attain heightened material loadings. Herein, we utilize binder fibrillation method to prepare 5 kinds of thickness cathode, the research shows that the dry electrode exhibits a capacity retention of 51.7%, surpassing the 44.3% retention of the traditional wet-based electrode at a loading of roughly $30 mg \mathbf{c m}^{-2}\left(4 \mathrm{mAh} / \mathrm{cm}^{2}\right)$ and is also capable of performing at ultra-high loadings up to $100 \mathrm{mg} \mathrm{cm}{ }^{-2}$ ($20 \mathrm{mAh} / \mathrm{cm}^{2}$). This exceptional cycling endurance can be attributed to a robust, interconnected binder fiber by air mill and enhanced mechanical attributes.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy Measurement Method for Fractional-Order Delay System Based on Model Predictive Control
abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) plays a crucial role in fuel cells (FCS) and can reflect the health status of fuel cells. The measurement of fuel cell EIS can apply ripple modulation on the control side of the DC/DC converter to obtain the ripple of the fuel cell output voltage and current. In practical control systems, since sampling is often a fractional-order delay, we have added a fractional-order delay compensation in the EIS measurement system. The experiment shows that this method can effectively solve the EIS of fuel cells.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Energy Harvesting System of The Electromagnetic Field around The Power Cords
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid energy harvesting system is proposed, which can harvest both the electric field energy and the magnetic field energy around the power cords. To realize the hybrid energy harvesting, a high voltage coupling capacitor (HVCC) is employed. On one hand, the electric filed energy can be induced through the capacitive coupling between the grounded tower and the power cords. On the other hand, the magnetic field energy is harvested by a current transformer (CT) device, and then tranferred to the grounded tower through the HVCC. Firstly, the overall system structure of the proposed system is presented. Secondly, the two energy harvesting modes are analyzed. Thirdly, simulation tests are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed system. The results show that the system is able to output at least 431 mW by harvesting only the electric field energy (no cord current case). Further more, the power transfer efficiency of the CT-harvested energy can be as high as 93.4%.

articleTitle: Research on Control Strategy of High-Voltage and High-Power Permanent Magnet Starter-Generator System for Aero-Engines
abstract: More/All electric aircraft (MEA) is the inevitable future development trend of the aviation industry. With the increase of electricity consumption in aircraft power systems, the voltage level of aviation high-voltage DC (HVDC) systems will exceed the current 270 V and then 540 V will be the future development target. This paper investigates the control strategy of 540 V HVDC permanent magnet integrated starter-generator system. Dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous machine (DTP-PMSM) is used to improve fault tolerance. The starting stage adopts the control strategy of constant torque first and constant power later, and the generation stage adopts fluxweakening combined with PWM controlled rectifier. Aiming at the problem of slow bus voltage response of traditional PI control in generation mode, this paper proposes to improve it by using sliding mode control (SMC) combined with extended state observer (ESO). Simulation verifies that the control strategy designed in this paper is feasible, and achieves stable control of the starter/generator system over a wide speed range of 4000~25000r/min.

Author Keywords: dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous machine

articleTitle: Short-Term Wind Power Prediction Based on GS-PCA-RF
abstract: At present, wind power generation is increasingly widely used because of its pollution-free and renewable advantages. Many appropriate methods is used to predict wind power in order to enhance the utilization rate of wind power. In this paper, a combined model wind power prediction method based on Grid Search(GS), Principal Component Analysis(PCA), and Random Forest(RF) is proposed. Firstly, the feature dimension reduction is carried out for the original data, the PCA is applied to reconstruct the original data, and the data after dimension reduction is trained. Then RF is used to learn the data, and the grid search algorithm is applied to select appropriate parameters of RF to reduce the influence of RF parameters on the training effect. Finally, the RF model optimized by grid search is employed to learn and predict the data. The combined prediction method based on GS-PCA-RF proposed in this paper is applied to the actual wind farm data, which obtains a better prediction effect in the short-term prediction of single unit and multi-unit and has a lower running time.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimal Configuration Strategy for Auxiliary Power Consumption in Sodium-Ion Energy Storage Power Stations
abstract: To address the optimization of auxiliary power configuration for sodium-ion energy storage power stations, this study proposes an efficient strategy. Initially, the characteristics of sodium-ion batteries are thoroughly examined, and various auxiliary power supply schemes are evaluated based on the operational requirements of energy storage stations. Subsequently, an optimization model is constructed with the goal of minimizing comprehensive losses, enabling rapid and accurate determination of auxiliary power supply plans and configuration values for sodium-ion energy storage power stations. Finally, practical case analysis confirms the significant advantages of centralized auxiliary power design in reducing system losses, decreasing failure rates, and enhancing operational efficiency, providing robust theoretical and practical support for the auxiliary power configuration of sodium-ion energy storage power stations.

articleTitle: Planning and Configuration of Hydrogen Production from Renewable Energy Considering On-grid/Off-grid Scenarios
abstract: With the proposal of the “ 3060 “ goal and the new type of power system, hydrogen energy, as a link to renewable energy and an energy storage medium, is expected to play an important role in the new type of power system in the future. This article first proposes a renewable energy hydrogen production system and constructs three typical on-grid/off-grid scenarios: residual electricity selling scenario, grid combined scenario, and off-grid scenario. The characteristics and operating strategies of these scenarios are described. To explore the operational characteristics of systems in different scenarios, a planning and configuration model for hydrogen production systems from renewable energy was constructed based on an improved multi-objective salp swarm algorithm, with the objectives of minimizing the total system cost, maximizing renewable energy utilization, and minimizing load shortage. Taking hydrogen production from a renewable energy project in the northwest region as an example, the model was solved and the effectiveness of the algorithm was verified. The results showed that the total cost of the grid combined scenario was the lowest, and electric hydrogen production could operate stably. The off-grid scenario has the lowest load shortage rate and operates stably under specific supporting power supply conditions. The renewable energy utilization rate is the highest in the scenario of residual electricity selling. Still, the total cost is relatively high, and the electric hydrogen production device cannot operate stably. This article provides a reference for the scenario selection, planning, and configuration of hydrogen production from renewable energy projects, which can improve the consumption of renewable energy, and reduce system costs and load shortage rate.

articleTitle: A Multi-physics Coupling Estimation Approach for the State of Charge of Lithium Batteries in All-Electric Aircraft
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are the sole energy supply for all-electric aircraft (AEA), their State of Charge (SOC) estimation is challenged by extreme temperature fluctuations, varying power loads, and mechanical stresses during flight. Inaccurate SOC estimation can lead to battery depletion and safety risks. This paper proposes an electro-thermal-mechanical multi-physics coupling approach for SOC estimation in aviation lithium batteries, developing a Differential Evolution (DE) algorithm for model parameter optimization and an Adaptive Extended Kalman Filter for improved accuracy. Experimental results show the proposed method achieves a SOC estimation error of less than 2.7% under extreme conditions.

articleTitle: Study on Lightning Performance of UHV Project in High Altitude Area
abstract: In this study, the characteristics of lightning parameters along a typical high-altitude UHV (Ultra High Voltage) transmission project are statistically analyzed, and the distribution law of lightning activity and a series of key lightning parameters along the line are obtained. According to the lightning activity characteristics and engineering design conditions of the line corridor in typical high-altitude areas, the lightning performance simulation analysis of 1000 kV transmission lines and substations along the line in high altitude areas is carried out based on the electromagnetic transient simulation program. The lightning trip-out rate level along the high-altitude areas and the whole line of the project and the lightning invasion wave overvoltage level of 1000 kV substations in high-altitude areas are obtained. Finally, the arrangement method of arrester in 1000 kV substation is put forward, and the lightning protection design scheme of the whole project and the insulation coordination scheme of the equipment in the station are checked. The research results provide technical support for engineering design and safe operation.

articleTitle: Coil Design and Analysis for High-Quality Thin Wireless Power Transfer Systems
abstract: To develop thinner electronic devices with wireless charging, a thin coil design is necessary. We propose a coil structure that minimizes thickness and mitigates the increase in resistance due to proximity and skin effects to achieve the high efficiency wireless power transfer (WPT) systems. The proposed coil consists of multiple thin wires created by dividing a single copper wire, with their start and end points connected. To determine an appropriate coil structure, various coil designs are compared using simulation software based on the finite element method. The proposed coil features ideal number of turns, inner diameter, copper wire width, and number of divisions optimized by a deep neural network (DNN) to achieve the highly efficient WPT systems under the specified power conditions. Simulation results show that for a coil with an outer diameter of 44 mm, copper wire thickness of 0.1 mm, coil distance of 2 mm, and frequency of 120 kHz, the proposed design improves the quality factor Q from 14.8 to 22.0, a 49% increase compared with a nondivision coil. Consequently, the power transfer efficiency increased from $\mathbf{8 5. 4 \%}$ to $\mathbf{9 0. 0 \%}$.

articleTitle: Analysis of Circular Couplers in Capacitive Power Transfer
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) technology is expected to be applied to a wide range of products. Currently, inductive coupling is mainstream, but capacitive coupling is attracting attention from the perspective of misalignment and EMI. In capacitive power transfer (CPT) systems, circular couplers, which have no horizontal directivity, can be used for wireless charging in a variety of situations. In this paper, we propose the optimum ratio of plate sizes for CPT systems of ringtype and vertical-type couplers. In addition, we clarify the difference in electrical characteristics between ring-type and vertical-type couplers. The analysis results of CPT systems with LC compensation show that the optimum size ratios for ring-type and vertical-type couplers are 0.7 and 0.6, respectively.

articleTitle: Multi-Component Mixed Oil with Transformer Typical Material Compatibility Analysis
abstract: Mixed insulation oil can complement the performance advantages of different oils and can be directly applied to existing mineral oil transformers without changing the transformer structure, which is an important development direction of high voltage and large capacity transformers. The compatibility study of mixed insulation oil and typical transformer materials has important significance for transformer design and operation. In this paper, we investigated the compatibility of multi-component mixed oil (MCMO) with typical transformer materials, and analyzed the changes in color, viscosity, relative dielectric constant, dielectric loss factor, volume resistivity, breakdown voltage, acid value, and interfacial tension parameters of MCMO before and after thermal aging. The results show that the MCMO has good compatibility with iron block, silicon steel sheet, enameled wire and epoxy plate, and the MCMO showed remarkable stability in kinematic viscosity, relative dielectric constant and breakdown voltage. But it has some compatibility problem with nitrile rubber.

articleTitle: A Battery State of Charge Algorithm with Observer for Engineering Application
abstract: This paper describes an observer algorithm to supersede Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) algorithm to calculate the state of charge (SOC) of battery, including: obtaining battery characteristic data and estimating the open circuit voltage (OCV), Filtering the estimated value with noise to obtain a filtered estimated value of the OCV. Through the operation and correction process of the established observer, the corrected SOC is obtained; Compared with the current mainstream EKF algorithm, the method described in this paper has clear logic and is convenient for upgrading individual functional modules, enhancing the practical application scope of dynamic correction SOC. Through the simplified design of the observer, it has the advantages of lightweight design while ensuring accuracy, making it more suitable for engineering implementation.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Day-Ahead Capacity Allocation Method for Shared Energy Storage in Multi-microgrid System
abstract: Shared energy storage (SES), with its cost-sharing and centralized management characteristics, provides an effective energy solution for modern power systems. To rationally allocate the day-ahead capacity of SES, this paper proposes a two-stage day-ahead capacity allocation method for SES in a multi-microgrid system (MMS). In the first stage, a day-ahead optimization scheduling plan for microgrids considering SES is developed. The objective is to minimize the daily operating cost of the MMS while considering constraints such as power balance, SES, and photovoltaics. In the second stage, SES capacity trading is conducted based on the scheduling results from the first stage. The actual charge and discharge power of SES capacity of each microgrid in MMS is calculated, and then SES capacity transaction is carried out between microgrids. The objective of the second stage is to minimize the overall transaction cost of the MMS while considering microgrid storage capacity and capacity trading constraints as conditions. Extensive evaluations were conducted on an MMS consisting of three microgrids. The results show that compared to distributed energy storage, this method reduces the total operating cost by $\mathbf{2 . 7 \%}$, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed two-stage day-ahead capacity allocation method for SES in an MMS.

articleTitle: Test and analysis of vibration reduction effect of indoor test system based on reactor vibration reduction and isolation device
abstract: In order to evaluate the indoor vibration isolation performance of the reactor’s vibration isolation reduction device, we have introduced a novel indoor simulation testing system. This system assesses the effectiveness of vibration isolation by analyzing the acceleration response and spectral curves at corresponding points on the upper and lower levels of the vibration isolation platform. Additionally, we have introduced a new parameter to quantify the damping effect within the enclosure. The new indoor simulation testing system consists of an electromagnetic shaker, a vibration isolation system, and a foundation platform. It simulates the actual operating conditions of the reactor by generating time-domain signals of vibration acceleration, which are collected from field tests and reproduced via the reactor’s electromagnetic shaker. The study results indicate that the reactor’s vibration-damping device significantly attenuates the transmission of vibrations to the surrounding environment. The new simulation testing system demonstrates excellent replication capabilities, aligning test data with field data. Furthermore, the evaluation of the reactor’s vibration-damping effect through the reduction in vibration levels is efficient, offering valuable insights to engineering designers for predicting the damping performance of the vibration isolation device and planning field tests.

articleTitle: Fault routing method for distribution networks based on variational mode decomposition and chaotic oscillator
abstract: This study proposes a method for fault section identification in distribution networks based on variational mode decomposition (VMD) and chaotic oscillators to address the difficulty of effectively identifying electricalcharacteristic quantities during single-phase ground faults. First, the zero-sequence current signals of each line are processed through the VMD algorithm, yielding a series of intrinsic mode functions. Second, an excellent denoising and smoothing model is established to balance the contradictory characteristics of waveform similarity and smoothness. Optimal intrinsic mode functions are chosen to realize the smooth processing of zero-sequence current signals. Finally, the smoothened zero-sequence current signals are inputted into a chaotic oscillator system to obtain phase portraits for each line. Furthermore, the chaotic state of the phase portraits is determined by calculating the Euclidean distance of image texture parameters, enabling fault section identification. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed method is unaffected by factors such as transient resistance, fault closing angle, and noise interference, and it has a high accuracy rate for fault section identification.

articleTitle: Kinetic Modelling of Hydro-Processed Renewable Jet Fuel Combustion in a Constant Volume Combustion Chamber
abstract: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is anticipated to play a crucial role in achieving the ‘Fly Net Zero’ target. Hydro-processed renewable jet (HRJ) is a certified SAF that can be blended with conventional jet fuel as a drop-in replacement. This study focuses on developing a reduced kinetic model for the combustion of HRJ fuel in a constant volume combustion chamber (CVCC) using CHEMKIN-PRO. The simulations are performed using the zero-dimensional (0-D) closed homogeneous batch reactor (CHBR) model. The objective is to formulate a surrogate model with simplified chemistry suitable for CVCC applications. The detailed kinetic mechanism employed in this study comprises 307 species which has been extensively validated against experimental data. Various strategies for kinetic reduction are explored using the Reaction Workbench in CHEMKIN-PRO to formulate a 3-component fuel surrogate, and the resulting simplified kinetic chemistries are compared. Ultimately, a reduced HRJ fuel surrogate model consisting of 111 species and 823 reactions is developed, demonstrating an $8.7 \%$ deviation in ignition time compared to the detailed counterpart. It is found that the ignition delay decreases with increasing initial temperature and pressure. However, equivalence ratios of 0.8, 1.0, and 1.2 show no significant differences in ignition time within the studied range. Apart from these, the reduced kinetic model is able to reproduce the mole fraction profiles of the key reactant and intermediate species when compared to the detailed model.

articleTitle: Assessing the Variable Harmonic Impedance Based on Bayesian Linear Regression
abstract: The existing approaches for assessing the utility harmonic impedance (UHI) cannot deal with the variable UHI. In fact, there are a variety of factors that may cause variations in UHI, including capacitor switching, filter switching, and operation adjustments in power grids. In regard to this problem, we propose a novel noninvasive approach for the estimation of UHI based on the Bayesian linear regression (BLR) that allows the variations of UHI to be precisely tracked. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by numerical simulations, and the results show that the performance of the proposed approach is much better than the existing approaches in tracking UHI with large-scale variations.

articleTitle: Method for predicting the demand for energy metering materials based on weight allocation
abstract: In response to the problem of poor performance in predicting the demand for electric energy metering materials and the need for a large amount of computing resources in existing technologies, this paper proposes a weight allocation based method for predicting the demand for electric energy metering materials. Starting from the annual consumption, the method gradually assigns weights to each month, unit, and type of materials. Suitable for calculating the material consumption of power supply stations in various situations, with a simple and reliable calculation method that meets both the annual forecast for procurement needs and the monthly forecast for delivery.

articleTitle: Optimization Method of Unit Recovery Path Considering Line Windage Yaw After Typhoon
abstract: For the unit recovery plan during black start, existing literature mainly focuses on minimizing system recovery time and maximizing power generation as objective functions. Few studies consider the damage to lines before recovery and the probability of line warning during the recovery process. This paper proposes a unit recovery path optimal selection method that considering line windage yaw Rate after extreme weathers. First, the minimum air clearance between the wire and the steel tower under different wind speeds can be obtained through simulating the wind speed during the typhoon, and the yaw rate model is established based on this. Then, considering the unit startup characteristics, recovery time, and operational constraints, taking the windage yaw rate as the line weight value. the Dijkstra algorithm is applied to get the shortest windage yaw rate of path each unit, The relationship between the path windage yaw rate and the recovery time is fully considered in order to minimize the unit recovery time under the premise of the lowest windage yaw rate. Finally, the proposed method is proved to be able to bypass the fault line and improve the success rate of the system recovery by using the IEEE 39 bus system and the actual power system in Guangdong province which means the method is scientific and effective.

articleTitle: A Sensitivity Analysis-based Method For Optimal Allocation of High-capacity Dynamic Voltage Restorers in Radial Distribution Networks
abstract: Overloading some nodes in a complex radial distribution network can lead to serious voltage deviation problems. Configuring a large-capacity dynamic voltage restorer is an effective measure to solve the node voltage offset problem. This paper proposes an optimization method for configuring highcapacity dynamic voltage restorers based on sensitivity analysis, which can quickly and reasonably select the installation location and capacity of high-capacity dynamic voltage restorers in the distribution network. It can quickly solve the installation location and capacity of large-capacity dynamic voltage restorers. Considering the vertical and horizontal structure of the radial distribution network, a governance model that focuses on vertical governance is proposed and supplemented by horizontal governance. First, the sensitivity of the large-capacity dynamic voltage restorer is calculated for all nodes using sensitivity analysis methods. In this way, the installation position of the large-capacity dynamic voltage restorer is obtained. Second, the sum of the absolute values of the voltage offset at the nodes of the radial distribution network is taken as the objective function. Establish a large-capacity dynamic voltage restorer capacity-optimized model. Finally, the optimization model is solved by improving the particle swarm algorithm. A case study was conducted on a 41-node radial system. The simulation results verify the rationality and effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Research on Online Evaluation and Optimization of Power Supply Reliability Considering Electric Vehicle Based Virtual Energy Storages
abstract: Electric vehicle is one of the important ways to achieve the goal of “dual carbon”. The disorderly charging behavior of EV has strong randomness in time and space, and its charging load will change the variation trend of daily load, which will affect the reliability of distribution network. This paper first analyzes the influence of EV on the reliability, and puts forward a reliability evaluation model of distribution network considering EV. Then, an online evaluation method of distribution network reliability based on real-time data is proposed from the two aspects of real-time operating status and reliability online evaluation efficiency. The power supply reliability index is obtained by loop search method based on load point, and finally verified by simulation.

Author Keywords: electric vehicle based virtual energy storages

articleTitle: A Partly-Isolated Three-Port DC-DC Converter for Hybrid Energy Storage Applications
abstract: In this paper, a novel partly-isolated three-port DC-DC converter (PITPDC) for hybrid energy storage system is proposed. The simplified system architecture leads to reduced cost and size by integrating battery and supercapacitor into the converter. Power distribution and optimization among multiple ports are achieved by the double phase-shift modulation strategy. The operating principle of the converter is analyzed, and its operation in different operating modes is discussed in details. The relationship between transmitted power and modulation parameters of each port is obtained. The experimental results demonstrate that the modulation parameters of the PITPDC can be adjusted to realize effective power distribution among different ports while maintaining the same output power. The proposed PITPDC enhances the flexibility and stability of the energy storage system and provides an effective technological solution for the integration of renewable energy and energy storage systems.

articleTitle: Short-Term Wind Power Prediction Based on KNN-BiGRU
abstract: Wind power generations have received widespread concern recently, however, due to the continuity of time series, ordinary machine learning models cannot learn the dependencies of continuous time series data well. To better predict the time series and improve the prediction effect of wind power, a shortterm wind power prediction method based on K-Nearest Neighbor(KNN) and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit(BiGRU) is proposed. Firstly, KNN is used to detect outliers in the wind speed-power sequence in the field collected data, and then the wind speed value of all abnormal data is modified to the mean value of wind speed. Then the modified data is input to the bidirectional gated recurrent unit for prediction. The bidirectional gated recurrent unit can efficiently learn the context information of the data and improve the prediction effect. The experimental results show that the proposed prediction method based on KNN-BiGRU obtains a good prediction effect on a single unit. Compared with other methods, it has the best prediction effect on multi-unit where the accuracy rate is $\mathbf{8 4. 3 0 4} \%$.

articleTitle: Combined-Vector Model Predictive Current Control for PMSM Based on Speed Difference
abstract: According to the number of voltage vectors used in the control period, the model predictive current control (MPCC) of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) can be divided into single-vector-based MPCC (SV-MPCC), double-vector-based MPCC (DV-MPCC) and three-vector-based MPCC (TV-MPCC). The average switching frequency, algorithm computation time and steady-state performances of the three control methods are different. So, each method has its own advantages and disadvantages. This paper presents combined vector MPCC (CV-MPCC), which makes use of the advantages of the three methods and can improve the overall performance of the drive system. Firstly, one method is selected based on operating state, which is determined by difference between the given speed and the actual speed. If the speed difference is greater than the threshold, the system is considered to be in dynamic state; otherwise, it is in steady state. Then, SV-MPCC method is applied when the system is in the dynamic state, and DV-MPCC or TV-MPCC method is adopted when the system is during the steady state. Finally, the experimental results verify the method.

articleTitle: Power Quality Disturbances Classification Based on CNN Combining Knowledge Distillation and Incremental Learning
abstract: With the integration of renewable energy sources and new power electronic devices, power grid complexity has increased, leading to frequent power quality disturbances. Existing classification models often require retraining when dealing with new disturbance types, resulting in long update periods and significant use of computing resources. This paper proposes the FKDIL-CNN, a convolutional neural network model that combines knowledge distillation and incremental learning, enabling the enabling rapid adaptation to new disturbances without requiring full retraining. The FKDIL-CNN transfers identification knowledge for the known old types from a high-accuracy teacher model to the student model. By introducing a dynamic weight mechanism to improve the traditional knowledge distillation loss function, the student model efficiently distills old knowledge from the teacher model and performs incremental learning on new knowledge. Compared with the existing methods, our proposed FKDIL-CNN significantly reduces the training time and computing resource consumption while maintaining high classification accuracy. Additionally, this model demonstrates strong noise immunity, making it a practical solution for PQDs monitoring in complex power grid.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Metal Oxide Surge Arrester in Complex Environment
abstract: Monitoring the leakage current of surge arrester can find its defects in time, which is of great significance to the security and stability of power system. But the complex environment will increase the difficulty of on-line monitoring the leakage current of surge arrester. Based on the equivalent circuit, the surge arrester is modeled and simulated by MATLAB Simulink software. The effects of surface contamination, voltage harmonics, voltage fluctuation and deterioration on the leakage current of surge arrester are studied. This paper summarizes the influence of different conditions on capacitive component, resistive component, amplitude, phase and harmonic of arrester leakage current, which lays a foundation for the online monitoring of surge arrester leakage current.

articleTitle: Parameter Identification of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Physics-Informed Neural Network
abstract: In this paper, the physical model of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is established by considering the influence of nonlinear factors such as magnetic saturation and cross-coupling, and the relationship between $d q$-axis flux and current is established by polynomial fitting, so as to establish a universal motor high-precision model. Then the parameters in the motor model are identified by the physics-informed neural network (PINN). In this new framework, the complexity of the motor high-precision model can be changed according to the actual situation of the motor. At the same time, the excellent fitting ability of neural network is fully utilized in PINN, and the accuracy of parameter identification is effectively enhanced by combining with the physical model of the motor. Finally, the identification accuracy of PINN for motor high-precision model are verified by simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation Research of Electromagnetic-electronic Hybrid Distribution Transformer
abstract: With the development of the power system, the requirements for the performance of distribution transformers are increasing day by day. Traditional transformers have problems such as poor voltage regulation performance and easy voltage overrun, which seriously affect the stability and quality of power supply, which brings challenges to the safe and reliable operation of the power grid. This paper proposes an electromagnetic-electronic hybrid distribution transformer, which combines a traditional transformer and a partial power electronic converter to solve the problems of poor voltage regulation performance and voltage overrun of the traditional transformer. Meanwhile, this paper introduces its system theory, including the design method of multi-winding electromagnetic transformers and the topology and control structure of power electronic converters. This paper also constructs an AC-DC-AC converter voltage regulation system based on fully controlled power semiconductor devices, which regulates the voltage by PWM pulse width modulation of the rectifier-inverter circuit. Simulation results confirm the feasibility of the designed electromagnetic-electronic hybrid distribution transformer.

articleTitle: Study of High-Frequency AC Discharge Phenomena Based on a Tesla Coil System*
abstract: This study is based on a Tesla coil discharge experimental platform, combined with high-speed imaging technology, to investigate the development process of AC discharge arcs. Through experiments with multiple groups of different gap lengths, the branching behavior, brightness characteristics, and current waveform changes of the AC arc discharge were analyzed. The results show that when arc branching occurs, the branches are denser near the high-voltage side, and the branches generally extend simultaneously until the main discharge path is formed, after which all branches disappear together. The brightness of the discharge arc exhibits a “double peak” characteristic, with the first peak corresponding to the formation of the main discharge path. Subsequently, the brightness undergoes a dimming and then brightening process, finally fading gradually after the second peak. The waveform of the grounding current can be divided into three phases: the sinusoidal spike phase, the peak phase, and the sinusoidal attenuation phase. The number of steps in the leader development of AC discharge corresponds to the number of peak drops in the current waveform. This study provides new methods and theoretical support for a deeper understanding of the microscopic process of AC high-voltage discharges.

articleTitle: Expansion Transition Speed of PMSM under MTPA Control Strategy Based on Improved Voltage Loop Quasi-Z Source Inverter
abstract: Maximum Torque Per Ampere (MTPA) control strategy effectively enhances the efficiency of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs), widely applied to extend the driving range of electric vehicles. However, as the battery discharges, the DC bus voltage of the inverter decreases gradually, limiting the switching frequency of the MTPA control strategy due to the voltage limit circle constraint. This reduction affects the acceleration performance and uphill climbing capability of electric vehicles. To address this issue, a novel control strategy is proposed. It introduces a Quasi-Z source network into the PMSM inverter and utilizes the rate of change of phase current amplitudes of the PMSM as a compensating factor in the voltage loop control of the Quasi-Z source network. This forms a positive feedback voltage loop control structure, enhancing the DC bus voltage and its dynamic response performance, thereby improving the switching frequency and extending the operating range of the PMSM. MATLAB/Simulink simulations and experimental validations demonstrate the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Operator-economical optimal scheduling considering peak-to-valley spread gains of energy storage stations
abstract: This paper proposes to sell power operator to configure energy storage plant to meet customer load demand by purchasing power from power producers. In order to respond positively to the national policy, for renewable energy generation, the operator adopts the strategy of priority pricing purchase. In order to verify the role of energy storage plant in peak and valley arbitrage, thermal power units adopt marginal cost pricing, which forms a price difference with the selling price of electricity, enabling the operator to obtain the price difference revenue through the energy storage plant. The result proves that under this power purchase and sale model, in a typical day, the operator is able to gain an additional 13622.4CNY through the energy storage plant.

articleTitle: A Quantitative evaluation method of new energy voltage support capability based on improved whitening weight function clustering
abstract: The high proportion of wind farms connected to the local power grid may impact voltage stability. While existing grid codes and technical standards have addressed this issue and introduced relevant solutions, primarily relying on wind farm control during voltage disturbances. Effectively assessing the voltage support from wind farms remains challenging. This paper proposes a new assessment method that not only comprehensively considers potential influencing factors of voltage support ability but also provides quantitative assessment results to support grid operators’ decisions. This paper considers impacts from both wind farm and grid sides, which mainly include wind farm and grid parameters and operational conditions. Based on these factors, the paper establishes a comprehensive wind farm voltage support capacity assessment index system. Finally, an improved sinusoidal whitening weight function is proposed to quantitatively solve the weighted assessment index system.

articleTitle: Two-stage Optimization Scheduling of Distribution Networks Considering Power Quality
abstract: This paper presents a novel two-stage optimization model for the scheduling of distributed generation (DG) in distribution networks, aiming to minimize operating costs and improve electricity quality. In the first stage, the model optimizes DG dispatch, considering factors such as market electricity prices, generation unit selection, and flexible load contract pricing. The second stage focuses on reactive power optimization, adjusting DG outputs and reactive power compensating devices to maintain voltage stability and reduce active power losses. To enhance the optimization process, an Hour-related particle swarm optimization (Hour-related PSO) algorithm is integrated, which leverages the continuity of optimal solutions between stages to accelerate convergence and reduce computational complexity. Simulations using the IEEE 33-node test system demonstrate that the proposed model, combined with Hour-related PSO, significantly lowers operational costs while improving voltage regulation and overall network performance. The results highlight the effectiveness of the approach in achieving optimal, cost-efficient dispatch and enhanced grid stability.

articleTitle: Optimization Study of Heater Water Level Finding in Thermal Power Units Based on Fuzzy Weighting and LSTM Deep Learning
abstract: In order to solve the problems of low efficiency, over-reliance on experience and insufficient adaptability under unknown working conditions, which generally exist in the heater water level control when thermal power units are flexibly peaking, combining the big data processing technology and deep learning, we firstly carry out the correlation analysis of each parameter that affects the heat return system, and according to the Pearson’s correlation coefficient, we identify the key parameters that have a significant impact on the energy consumption of the heat return system. For these important parameters, the operating state of the heater system is divided by Fuzzy C-means (FCM) clustering algorithm, and the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network is used to construct the optimal value model of the heater water level for the divided typical conditions, and based on the fuzzy weighted real-time condition matching Based on the fuzzy-weighted real-time working condition matching mechanism, the real-time data of the heater system under different boundary conditions are matched with the model to complete the optimization of the heater water level.

articleTitle: PCC voltage feed-forward robust control strategy of grid-connected converter under complex conditions
abstract: The grid-connected operation of the converter is easily affected by the background harmonics of the power grid voltage and the complex operating conditions of the power grid impedance, which will not only cause the output current to distort, but even cause the converter to oscillate and cannot operate stably. Through the analysis of the equivalent impedance model of the converter, it can be seen that the main reason for the system instability is the low phase margin at the intersection frequency point of the grid impedance and the converter impedance amplitude, that is, the impedance ratio of the two cannot meet the Nyquist stability criterion. In this paper, a new impedance model is established by introducing the impedance stability criterion when the converter is connected to the power grid. The use of grid-connected point voltage feed-forward compensation control can greatly expands the passive frequency domain range of the impedance, and ensures that the converter can stably output the grid-connected current with high waveform quality under the influence of wide-range time-varying grid impedance. The simulation model is built in MATLAB. The active power of the load is 6 kW and the reactive power is 8 kVar. By setting different parameters, it is verified that the strategy has good operating characteristics in both high frequency band and low frequency band.

articleTitle: Supercritical Once-Through Boiler Modeling via Heat Current Method and Its Application in Primary Frequency Regulation
abstract: With the increasing integration of renewable energy, the demand for frequency regulation has become more pronounced. Coal-fired power plants, long considered the ballast of the modern power system, are now tasked with assuming a significant portion of regulation responsibilities. Nevertheless, current models tend to concentrate on the turbines, often neglecting the nonlinear dynamics associated with boilers and the influence of boiler heat storage on the regulation capacity of power units. Utilizing the heat current method, this study develops a dynamic model for the boiler of thermal power units and incorporates it into the frequency regulation framework. The result indicates that the proposed model achieves a 62.7% reduction in average simulation error under the scenario of prolonged and high-capacity power deficiencies of the power grid.

articleTitle: Design and Electromagnetic Simulation Analysis of a New Type of Radial-Axial Hybrid Flux Motor
abstract: In the development process of electric aircraft and underwater propulsion systems, motors are required to have high torque density and specific power under weight/volume limitations. This artical proposes a novel radial-axial hybrid magnetic flux motor with high torque capability, which can meet the torque/power output requirements under inherent space constraints. The radial and axial magnetic forces are mixed and utilized, using a shaft radial surrounding anti leakage magnetic structure to reduce the phenomenon of magnetic leakage, realizing the axial application of radial magnetic leakage and the radial application of axial magnetic leakage, improving the utilization rate of permanent magnets. The mutual insertion of axial and radial stators reduces the axial size of the motor, resulting in a small volume. The dual axis stator has high power, concentrated force, and high power density of the motor, effectively reducing the volume and weight of the rotor component. The rotor of the proposed radial axial hybrid flux motor consists of three rotor parts, namely radial rotor and axial double rotor. The stator is designed as a three sided slot structure, surrounded by three rotor parts, ultimately forming a three sided air gap structure. And simulation verification was carried out through finite element analysis.

articleTitle: Adaptive Power Distribution Method Considering Lifespan Synchronization of Multi-Stack Fuel Cell Power Systems
abstract: To extend the lifespan of multi-stack fuel cell power systems (MS-FCPS) and ensure that the overall aging of each stack remains consistent during operation, an adaptive power distribution method considering life convergence is proposed for MS-FCPS. During the operation of MS-FCPS, the output power of fuel cells dynamically changes with different operating conditions, leading to inconsistent aging of each stack. Therefore, the State of Health (SOH) is proposed as a quantitative indicator to represent the aging degree of the fuel cell stacks during operation. Additionally, a semi-empirical model of the fuel cell is used to simulate the impact of aging on stack performance. Finally, a simulation experiment built with MATLAB compares the adaptive power distribution method with the average power distribution method and the chain power distribution method. The results show that this method can coordinate the output of each fuel cell, making the health state of each stack tend to be consistent, thereby extending the system’s lifespan.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Application Scenarios of Synchronous Condensers in Weak Electric Grids with Solar Energy Storage
abstract: With the large-scale integration of photovoltaic and energy storage systems into the grid, voltage and frequency stability issues have intensified, and the addition of synchronous condensers is being considered as a solution. However, the application of the“solar-storage + synchronous condenser” system in weak grid stations has certain limitations, as it may lead to power angle stability issues in some grids with weak network structures. This paper primarily explores the safety and stability characteristics of the combined solar-storage and synchronous condenser system, comparing the roles of the synchronous condenser under various factors, and proposes effective measures to improve power supply capacity in local weak grids.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of a Novel Stability Criterion Versus the Generalized Nyquist Stability Criterion in More-Electric Aircraft Cascaded System
abstract: As the power demands of onboard electrical equipment continue to rise, more-electric aircraft (MEA) power supply systems require an increasing number of converters to provide controlled voltage or frequency power. However, the extensive use of converters and their interaction with generators lead to instability in AC bus voltage, posing potential safety risks to aircraft. Therefore, analyzing the stability of cascaded systems consisting of generators and converters is crucial. This paper proposes a novel stability criterion based on the Gershgorin circle theorem to accurately assess the AC output voltage stability of MEA cascaded systems. Compared to the generalized Nyquist stability criterion (GNSC), the proposed method aligns more closely with the actual stability state of aircraft systems and allows for the pre-design customization of stability margins, providing valuable guidance for aircraft system design. Finally, simulations validate the advantages and accuracy of this method through comparative analysis.

articleTitle: Reliability Margin Decision Method of Multi-region Transmission Channel Based on Depth Deterministic Strategy Gradient
abstract: In order to optimize the decision-making model of multi-region transmission channel margin, the optimal decision-making model aiming at the maximum net income of each region is first constructed, and then the decision-making physical model of multi-region transmission channel margin is constructed considering the influence of uncertainties such as wind power and load fluctuation. In view of the high and continuous dimensions of the decision variables of the model, the multi-agent depth deterministic strategy gradient algorithm is used to solve the problem of slow convergence of traditional multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms. Finally, the simulation results of IEEE118 nodes verify the effectiveness of the multi-agent depth deterministic strategy gradient algorithm for solving multi-region TRM decision problems..

articleTitle: Study on regeneration and recovering of cathode materials for waste LFP batteries with sucrose
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries serve as indispensable energy storage devices in grid-scale energy storage systems, and the recycling of their LFP (lithium iron phosphate) batteries is of crucial significance in promoting efficient resource recycling, enhancing environmental protection, and effectively reducing the overall cost of energy storage systems. Current recovery methods via acid leaching are complex, costly, and environmentally harmful. We propose a simple, cost-effective, and eco-friendly method using sucrose for waste LFP material treatment. By dimethyl carbonate immersion and low-temperature sintering, followed by high-temperature calcination with lithium source and sucrose, the LFP material’s capacity was regenerated from $110 \mathrm{mAh} / \mathrm{g}$ to over $155 \mathrm{mAh} / \mathrm{g}$, with improved microstructure and lattice structure. Our findings suggest sucrose-assisted high-temperature solid-state recovery as a promising approach for high-performance regenerated LFP cathodes.

articleTitle: Motion Characteristics of Metal Particles and Dust Visualization Method for DC GIL/GIS
abstract: Particle pollution significantly compromises the safety and reliability of DC GIL and GIS equipment. Understanding the motion characteristics of particles is essential for addressing this issue. This paper presents the construction of a ±320 kV GIS equivalent test platform to investigate the motion characteristics of spherical particles, linear particles, and dust particles. Spherical particles exhibit reciprocating motion under the influence of the actuating voltage, while linear particles display more complex motion characteristics, including the occurrence of the firefly phenomenon and the standing phenomenon. Additionally, the dust location identification method, based on the Vibe algorithm, effectively identifies the dispersion phenomenon of dust in response to the applied voltage. This research offers a valuable reference for the design of main insulation systems aimed at mitigating particle movement.

articleTitle: Considering the dynamic pricing and optimization model of the stackelberg game in which independent energy storage operations participate
abstract: This paper proposes a dynamic pricing optimization method for microgrid operators based on Stackelberg game theory, taking into account the participation of independent energy storage operators. Firstly, optimization operation models for microgrid operators and users are established separately. Then, the game relationships among operators, independent energy storage operators, and load aggregators are analyzed, and a Stackelberg game model with operators as leaders is constructed, through which the optimal electricity-heat prices are obtained by optimization solution. Finally, case study analysis verifies that the proposed optimization method with independent energy storage participation can increase the overall profits of upper-level operators while achieving peak shaving and valley filling for some energy.

articleTitle: Technical requirements for performance evaluation and conformity assessment of DC collector systems for offshore wind farms
abstract: As a new transmission schemes, DC (Direct Current) grid-connected technology has many technical problems to be solved. Among them, in the case of offshore wind power DC transmission system, the transmission capacity is reduced and the active power regulation at the power supply terminal is slow, which will lead to the increase of the system voltage at the sending terminal and threaten the safe operation of the converter and offshore wind turbines at the sending terminal. Aiming at the transient overvoltage problem of traditional DC transmission system, many research results have been obtained and many measures have been put forward. For example, fast cut-off filter, additional control of DC control system, sacrificial arrester and large-capacity arrester are used to improve the voltage level of equipment. However, for offshore wind power transmission system, this problem is still in the preliminary research stage. Compared with the traditional DC transmission system, offshore wind power transmission system has its unique characteristics. Offshore wind turbines have reactive power regulation ability, and the transmission end of flexible direct drive system does not need to install filters, so the converter of flexible direct drive system responds faster. Therefore, it is necessary to master the data analysis technology of the evaluation index system of the DC collector system of offshore wind farms, and integrate the analytic hierarchy process, fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method and Hopfield network evaluation method, and put forward a comprehensive evaluation method of system performance combining multi-dimensional characteristic parameters to form a qualified evaluation scheme.

articleTitle: Inductive Power Decoupling Integrated Charging System for Electric Vehicles Based on a Switched Reluctance Motor
abstract: An integrated charging topology is proposed for electric vehicles based on Switched Reluctance Motors. In the charging mode, windings and part of the motor power converter are reused as a dual-diode bridgeless Boost PFC rectifier, and the remaining one phase and its bridge arm are reused as an inductive power decoupling circuit to absorb the power ripple of the bus and reduce the output voltage ripple.

articleTitle: Design of Multi-Channel Online Monitoring System for Conducted Interference in High-Speed Trains
abstract: Aiming at the conducted interference generated during the operation of high-speed trains, a multi-channel online monitoring system for conducted interference applicable to highspeed trains is designed. The monitoring system includes hardware and software design. The hardware module is selected according to the requirements, mainly including signal acquisition module, signal processing module and data transmission module. The software design adopts QT platform to realize the upper computer interface. An experimental platform is set up for verification, and the experimental results prove that the monitoring system can capture the transient interference signal, and the correlation coefficient with the real signal can reach 0.97, which meets the requirements of the train conducted interference monitoring.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of GIS Cable Terminal Defect Detection Based on Ultrasonic Method
abstract: The GIS cable terminal refers to a specialized joint used to connect gas-insulated metal-enclosed switchgear and cables. Within the GIS cable terminal, there are two composite interfaces: epoxy resin/rubber and rubber/XLPE. In low-temperature environments, the differing expansion rates between metal and epoxy resin can lead to defects at the joint surface, resulting in partial discharge and potentially catastrophic failures such as explosions. We employed ultrasonic testing methods for the detection of defects in GIS cable terminals by simulation study. By analyzing the waveform of the received ultrasonic signals, it is possible to ascertain the existence of internal defects within these terminals. The ultrasonic method demonstrates significant potential for effective defect detection in GIS cable terminals.

articleTitle: A Novel Submodule Voltage Balancing Control Strategy for iM2DCT in MVDC Distribution Network
abstract: The iM<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>DCT features high scalability and modularity, making it a key component in DC distribution networks.
