A critical challenge in controlling the iM<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>DCT is balancing the submodule (SM) capacitor voltages. However, the traditional methods cannot effectively balance the SMs’ voltage under non-unity voltage conversion ratio scenarios. To facilitate the iM<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> DCT’s operation range with balanced SMs’ voltage, this paper proposes a novel SM capacitor voltage balancing strategy by assigning the group signal pulses with the negative charge value in the descending order of SM voltage, followed by the distribution of phase-shift pulses with the positive charge value. The effectiveness and feasibility of this strategy are verified using a full-power MATLAB/Simulink model.

articleTitle: Manufacturing supervision and inspection of lithium battery energy storage equipment
abstract: Under the background of “carbon peak” and “carbon neutrality”, large-scale energy storage equipment is an important basic equipment to support the new power system. Lithium battery energy storage equipment has good commercialization and scale effect, and has become the main technical route of energy storage except pumped storage power stations. Lithium battery energy storage system has the characteristics of assembly line, mass production and short manufacturing cycle, and its intrinsic safety is relatively low. In this industry background, the traditional witness method of equipment manufacturing supervision is not only inadequate, but also difficult to find problems and inefficient. Based on the witness of manufacturing supervision, laboratory sampling inspection and on-site inspection after equipment installation can more comprehensively find the quality defects of energy storage equipment in the process of manufacturing, transportation and installation, and ensure the safe and reliable operation of the equipment.

articleTitle: Study on Frequency and Voltage Control of a Micro-grid with Renewable Energy based on Grid-forming Energy Storage System
abstract: This paper proposes a frequency and voltage control method for a micro-grid without supports of synchronous generators, based on virtual synchronous generator (VSG) method. Taking an actual remote micro-grid in north China as an example, a VSG control strategy for energy storage system(ESS) is designed, according to characteristics of loads, wind power stations and photovoltaic($\mathrm{P V}$) stations in the $\backslash$ micro-grid. The validity of the method is verified by electromagnetic transient simulations. The results show that with this control method the frequency and voltage regulation capacity of the micro-grid are improved, and as a result, the wind farms, PV stations and loads in the area can operate stably, improving the reliability of power supply in this area. The results of this paper provide important and valuable references for solving the week reliability of power supply of a micro-grid without supports of a synchronous generator.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Improvement of Grid-Forming Inverters During Grid Fault Considering Voltage Dynamic Characteristics
abstract: The grid-forming converter is extensively utilized in grid interfaces which has the ability to flexibly adjust voltage and frequency. However, the interactions among control loops during grid disturbances complicate the analysis of transient synchronous stability in current-limited conditions. In this paper, the transient stability of the grid-forming converter is studied, which not only completes the comprehensive and accurate characterization of the dynamic characteristics of the virtual synchronous machine under the virtual impedance control, but also illustrates the mechanism of the transient switching operation mode under the current limited state, which has the phenomenon of ineffective controller integration. Considering the influence of VSG main control parameters on the transient stability of the system, an improved fault crossing control strategy is proposed, which can effectively improve the transient stability and smooth switching degree. Finally, the correctness of the above theoretical analysis is verified by simulation

articleTitle: Active Thermal Control Algorithm for Si/SiC Hybrid Switch-Based Energy Storage Converter
abstract: This article proposed an active thermal control algorithm for the Si IGBT and SiC MOSFET hybrid switch (Si/SiC HyS). The thermal unbalance phenomenon of the Si/SiC HyS is illustrated in this paper. The different switching patterns and corresponding loss distribution characteristics and unbalanced device junction temperature distribution are analyzed. In order to conduct the research on active regulation of device junction temperatures, the therm al model of an energy storage Si/SiC HyS based converter is built. Different combinations of Si/SiC HyS switching patterns are analyzed and an active thermal control algorithm is proposed based on the switching pattern combination control. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is validated by simulation. It shows that by using the proposed algorithm, the thermal stress on SiC MOSFET device junction can be relieved, which can increase the device long term reliability and maximum output power capacity. The trade-off between efficiency and SiC MOSFET junction temperature is also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Improved Zero-Sequence Current Hysteresis Control With Reduced Switching Losses for Open-End Winding PMSM Drives With Common DC Bus
abstract: In this paper, a novel hybrid space vector modulation (SVM) modulation strategy is proposed to address the shortcomings of the existing zero-sequence current hysteresis control for open-end winding permanent magnet synchronous motor (OEW-PMSM), which can reduce the switching losses without decreasing the modulation range. The common DC bus type OEW-PMSM has gained widespread attention due to its advantages of high dc-link voltage utilization and large output capacity. However, this structure provides a zero-sequence current loop, which leads to hazards such as increased system operating losses and motor torque pulsations. Therefore, suppression of zero-sequence current needs to be considered. In this paper, a novel modulation strategy is proposed for two judgement modes, 6-sector and 12-sector. For different zero-sequence current and voltage vector positions, inverter alternating clamp and normal dual vector modulation are used in the corresponding modes respectively. This strategy can effectively reduce the switching frequency compared to the existing hysteresis control, and its voltage utilization is the same as using the middle hexagon space vector modulation. Finally, it is verified by MATLAB/Simulink simulation that the proposed method can effectively suppress the zero-sequence current and reduce the switching losses.

Author Keywords: open-end winding permanent magnet synchronous motor (OEW-PMSM)

articleTitle: Research on dynamic wireless power Transfer position detection technology for electric vehicles based on SSA-SVR
abstract: In order to solve the problem of the deviation and the switching of the working state of the transmitter during the driving of electric vehicles, a position detection technology using the multiplexing of the switching detection coil is proposed, and the offset of the vehicle is predicted by using the support vector regression method optimized based on the sparrow search algorithm(SSA-SVR), and the constant longitudinal position switching is realized by detecting the vehicle deviation and the switching detection system, and finally the detection accuracy of 5mm is realized.

articleTitle: Fault Ride-Through Strategy for MMC-Based MTDC System Integrated with Offshore Wind Farms to Reduce Dynamic Braking System
abstract: This paper developed an energy recovery method for modular multilevel converter-based multi-terminal direct current (MMC-MTDC) system integrated with offshore wind farms (OWFs) to achieve onshore AC fault ride-through. By using the capacitor energy margin of the MTDC system to recover the surplus power during onshore AC faults, the installation of the dynamic braking system (DBS) can be reduced. First, an energy coordination control strategy is developed to achieve synchronous regulation of the capacitor energy in multiple MMCs, while improving overall energy utilization efficiency. Then, preset DC voltage trajectories under two types of AC faults are designed to manage the capacitor energy in MMCs properly during AC faults. Finally, a simulation model of the four-terminal HVDC system integrated with OWFs was built in PSCAD/EMTDC to verify the effectiveness of the proposed energy recovery method.

articleTitle: A Study of the Effect of Grounding Network Node Topology on its Lightning Impact Characteristics
abstract: Due to the inductive effect of the grounding grid and the high-frequency characteristics of the lightning current, when the electrical equipment is struck by lightning, the potential of the grounding grid rises rapidly, which is easy to cause insulation damage to the electrical equipment. In this paper, a simulation model is established, and different topologies are used as the basic research objects, and the time-domain impact characteristics of different grounding conductors under different influencing factors are first analyzed. Secondly, the influence of the absence of some conductors and the location and number of conductor corrosion fractures on the impulse response voltage at different injection points is analyzed, and the judgment method of the shape of the underground conductor after the extreme fracture of the underground conductor structure is obtained, and the authenticity and reliability of the simulation are finally verified by experiments.

articleTitle: Active Security Constraint Identification Based on KKT Condition for Security-Constrained Economic Dispatch
abstract: The optimal power flow problem plays an essential role in power system economic dispatch. To conduct daily operation, a huge number of scheduling plans are made in diverse systems. In order to reduce the scale of economic dispatch problems and improve the efficiency of scheduling, an active security constraint identification method is proposed in this paper, which aims to remove adequate useless security constraints to accelerate the calculation of dispatch problem, and keep the optimal solution unchanged. Based on the KKT condition, the proposed model can search for every possible active security constraint, other inactive constraints will be removed for speeding up the solution process. Case studies of an IEEE 30-bus system are demonstrated to show the active constraint identification results. Then, a 57 -bus system and a 118 -bus system are used for presenting the calculation efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Improved Transformer Models Involved with Compensating Current Source for Transient Analysis
abstract: When a transformer undergoes transient processes such as overvoltage or closing, it experiences varying degrees of saturation, and the excitation current at the port can even increase to several times the rated current. The current power system simulation software usually expresses the nonlinear characteristics of transformers by setting a compensating current source in the T-type equivalent circuit of the transformer. The integration process and placement position of the compensation current source affect the simulation accuracy of transformer port inrush current. This paper improved the port flux calculation method when the compensating current source is placed on the excitation branch, primary side, or secondary side respectively. Moreover, numerical calculation expression of the port current and the magnetic linkage integral expression of the compensating current source are obtained. Then, $\mathrm{C}++$ language is used to establish numerical calculation programs for different compensation methods. Finally, by comparing the transient inrush currents obtained by different compensation methods with the simulation results of PSCAD, the impact of different compensation methods on the calculation of inrush currents is demonstrated, and the improvement methods of flux integration under different compensation methods are analyzed. The analysis and improvement of compensation methods proposed in this paper can provide a theoretical basis for improving the accuracy of transient analysis.

articleTitle: A Networked Method Applied to Sensitivity Analysis of a VSG controlled BESS System
abstract: The grid-forming battery energy storage system (BESS) plays important role in constructing new energy system. This paper presents a frequency domain modal-based stability analysis of virtual synchronous generator (VSG) controlled BESS. Both ac and dc side interactive dynamics of the grid-tied inverter system are considered, by establishing a hybrid ac/dc impedance network. Then, the frequency domain modal analysis (FMA) method for networked converter systems is applied to the BESS system, covering the eigen-sensitivity from the node level to parameter level. Using this method, key parameters that influence the BESS system’s weakly/negative damping modes most can be better analyzed and identified. The analysis results are validated via the time-domain simulations.

articleTitle: Large-Signal Stability Analysis of Low-Voltage Power Distribution System Considering Random Disturbance Intensity
abstract: The low-voltage power distribution system (LVPDS) may experience large-signal instability issues due to random power disturbances from distributed renewable energy sources and constant power loads. Firstly, a small-signal model of the LVPDS is established, which can be used to analyze changes in eigenvalues under different load powers. Secondly, a large-signal model of the LVPDS considering random disturbances is established using the Takagi-Sugeno modeling method. This large-signal model can be used to effectively evaluate changes in the largest estimated domain of attraction under different intensities of random disturbances. By comparing the eigenvalue trajectories and the largest estimated domains of attraction under different random disturbance intensities, an applicability criterion for small-signal models based on the maximum random disturbance intensity is proposed. Additionally, a method for solving the maximum random disturbance intensity based on the largest estimated domain of attraction is presented in this paper. Finally, the switching models of the LVPDS are constructed using PLECS software and the RT-box hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experimental platform, respectively. The validity of the constructed models and the proposed criterion is verified by multiple sets of simulation and experimental waveforms.

articleTitle: Multi-channel short-term electric load forecasting model based on CEEMD data decomposition
abstract: Aiming at the stochasticity and instability of power load data and the difficulty of traditional forecasting models to accurately capture the local and global features of the data, a multi-channel short-term power negative character model (CACCLA) based on CEEMD is proposed. Firstly, the method utilizes CEEMD to decompose the original load teachings into feature modal components representing the unused scales to reduce the instability of the original series; then, multi-features are introduced into each modal component after the decomposition, and the Bagging builds multiple models through self-sampling, it effectively reduces the variance of predictions and improves stability and accuracy.; and finally. The CNN-CBAM+LSTM-ATT model was used for load prediction. Through comparison experiments with several prediction models, the results show that the model has a better prediction effect than traditional prediction methods.

articleTitle: Online Estimation of Power Shortage in Power Systems Driven by Local Frequency Measurement Data
abstract: With the growing penetration of renewable generation, the inertia and frequency support ability of the, renewable-dominated power svstem are continuously reduced, which leads to frequency collapsewhen the system is disturbed. Therefore, it is of great significance to promptly and accurately evaluate the power shortage after a major disturbance to fill the power shortage quickly. This paper proposes an online estimation approach of power shortage in power system based on deep convolution and long short term memory composite neural network driven by local frequency measurement data. First, since using the synchronous measurements to obtain the frequency of center of inertia (COI) cannot adapt to the rapidity of online estimation, this paper employs the local frequency measurements to estimate the COI frequency, avoiding the delay effect caused by the complex communication. Then, it designs a deep composite neural network to mine the correlation information between massive frequency data and power shortage. Finally, it tests the simulations on a 39-bus system to verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach is effective and fast.

articleTitle: Smart Digital Inspection and Maintenance of Substations
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to substation inspection through the implementation of a smart digital inspection system that leverages advanced technologies, including real-time monitoring, cloud-based data processing, intelligent navigation, and anomaly detection. By equipping inspectors with mobile devices, the system enables efficient data collection and immediate access to critical information during inspections. The integration of real-time alerts and thermal defect detection facilitates prompt responses to equipment anomalies, enhancing operational reliability and safety. Additionally, the system promotes seamless data sharing across departments, significantly reducing coordination time and improving maintenance efficiency. The results highlight the transformative impact of digital technologies on substation management, ultimately contributing to a more resilient power grid.

articleTitle: Hybrid HVDC converter with fault current limiting capability
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid HVDC converter with fault current limiting copiability for the offshore wind power DC transmission system. By combining a diode rectifier and an auxiliary converter, the hybrid converter realizes low-cost and high-reliability power conversion. The auxiliary converter is also able to output negative voltage for current suppression during faults. By eliminating expensive DCCBs, the construction cost of offshore wind power is reduced. The analysis of topology and the operation modes of the hybrid converter are carried out. The fault current equations are deduced to reveal the fault current limiting principle. The fault protection strategy of the hybrid converter as well as high-speed switches are proposed. The verification of the feasibility of the hybrid HVDC converter with fault current limiting capability is conducted by simulations on MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Research on Control Technology of Substation Noise Based on Active Noise Reduction
abstract: In recent years, more and more urban substations have seriously affected the normal life of the surrounding residents, of which the most serious is the impact of substation noise on human health. Therefore, noise exceeding the standard has become an important problem to be solved by the substation. For the use of sound absorption, sound insulation of the traditional passive noise reduction methods for low-frequency noise control effect is not good, and may affect the ventilation and lighting, and active noise reduction in the noise control has many advantages, so this paper from the active control aspects of the start, based on the principle of acoustic phase cancellation interference of the active noise reduction technology to achieve the management of the substation noise, analyse the factors that will have an impact on the effect of noise reduction and through the simulation of the study concluded that It analyses the factors affecting the noise reduction effect and derives the noise reduction law of each influencing factor through simulation, and formulates the optimal noise reduction scheme, which is of great significance to the field of substation noise control.

articleTitle: Anticorrosive electronic fluorinated liquid as fire extinguishing agent for lithium-ion batteries safety
abstract: Perfluorohexanone (Novec 1230) is expected to be used as a special fire extinguishing agent for lithium-ion batteries. However, Novec 1230 contains trace moisture and HF, which will cause secondary damage to electrical. In this work, 1,1,2,2,3,3,4-heptafluorocyclopentane (HFC) was used as the cooperative fire extinguishing medium of Novec 1230, and a MOF with amino group (NH2-MIL-101-Ti) was used as the additive to remove the moisture and HF in the fire extinguishing agent. Through the actual lithium-ion battery fire extinguishing, cooling and insulation experiments, it is found that Novec 1230/HFC-MOF can extinguish the open fire of lithium-ion battery in 12s, reduce the temperature from $300{ }^{\circ} \text{C}$ to $150{ }^{\circ} \text{C}$ in 60s, and the electrical equipment can operate stably for a long time in the fire extinguishing agent immersion. The anti-corrosion fire extinguishing agent developed in this work can solve the fire safety problems in large-scale application of lithium-ion batteries.

articleTitle: Knowledge Mapping on the Research and Development of New Power System
abstract: Building an energy supply system centered around clean and low-carbon energy and constrcting a new power system (NPS) are key measures to achieve carbon neutrality goals. This article reviews references from the past 20 years related to new power system, based on the Web of Science (WOS) core collection database. It utilizes CiteSpace for a visual organization of the relevant data. Important milestones and research hotspots in the development process of new power system has been deeply analyzed. The results reveal that the research interest in the field of NPS is currently in an exponential growth phase; keywords like “renewable energy”, “optimization”, and “new energy” are among the most prominent besides “new power system”, and are at the forefront of research.

articleTitle: A simplified Jacobian matrix based fast continuous power flow calculation method considering capacity of frequency modulation units
abstract: Deep integration of distributed energy brings great uncertainty into distribution network. Therefore, fast continuous power flow calculation plays a vital role in helping distribution networks respond to system instability caused by dramatic changes in network power flow. This paper proposes a continuous power flow calculation method based on simplified Jacobian matrix, considering the capacity of frequency modulation(FM) units in the actual operation process, which provides a timely reference for the safe operation of the system and the unbalanced power distribution. The results of case study indicate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method from the perspective of power system stable operation.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of Single-phase Multistage DC-AC Inverter with Medium-frequency Transformer Isolated DC/DC Converters
abstract: With the advancement of power electronics technology and the growing demand of renewable energy harness, solid-state transformer (SST), as an emerging transformer technology, has garnered significant attention. This paper proposes a control strategy based on state space averaging method (SSAM) for a DC/AC converter formed by two parts, one being mediumfrequency transformer isolated DC/DC converters while the other being single-phase multistage DC-AC inverter. The first part in such a SST is controlled by comparison of reversed triangular waveforms with the same reference signal to produce two pairs of switching signals. For the second part in the SST, the same circuit topology is controlled by two different methods to make it work as a current-controlled voltage source inverter or a voltage-controlled voltage source inverter. MATLAB was utilized to validate the proposed theory. The modeling results demonstrate that the proposed control method effectively enhances the stability of these structures while ensuring balanced output voltage across each of multistage in the single-phase inverter.

articleTitle: Method of increasing equivalent damping in DC voltage synchronous control based on additional low-pass filter feedback
abstract: Based on Direct Voltage Synchronization Control (DVSC), the grid-forming converter can stabilize the DC side voltage while achieving self-synchronization. However, traditional DVSC only simulates the inertia of synchronous machines and cannot emulate damping, which can lead to lowfrequency oscillations. To examine the similarities and differences between DVSC and synchronous machines, this paper analyzes their equivalent relationships. Based on the analysis of low-frequency oscillation mechanisms, an improved DVSC control method with an additional low-pass filter feedback loop is proposed to achieve damping simulation effects similar to those of synchronous machines. In the end, the effect of the proposed method is verified through simulations.

articleTitle: A Real-time Linkage Preparation Method for Unit Interconnection Line Planning Considering Safety Constraints and Allocation Principles
abstract: Through thorough field research and based on actual needs, a real-time linkage method for compiling unit connection line plans considering safety constraints and allocation principles has been proposed. This method not only enables unified management of the start stop plan and corresponding connection line plans of pumping and storage units in the North China region, but also enables automatic modification of the corresponding provincial network connection line plan values according to the capacity allocation ratio under any start-up mode of pumping and storage units, and issues them for execution. At the same time, it considers unit output constraints, unit ramp rate constraints, unit ramp constraints, unit start stop constraints, connection line power and ramp constraints, etc.

articleTitle: Improvement of Fractional-Order Sliding Mode Control in Hydrogen Fuel Cell Grid-Connected Systems Based on RBF Algorithm
abstract: In recent years, there has been widespread attention on integrating new energy sources such as hydrogen fuel cells into microgrids. This article proposes an improved fractional sliding mode control for a hydrogen fuel cell grid-connected system based on the RBF algorithm. Firstly, establishing a mathematical model of the hydrogen fuel cell, its input characteristics and power characteristics are analyzed. Then, the fractional-order sliding mode control (FOSMC) algorithm is used to track the grid-connected current and obtain the control rate. To reduce chattering and enhance the system’s robustness, the RBF algorithm is used to improve the fractional-order sliding mode, allowing the sliding mode parameters to be adjusted based on the actual output error. Finally, simulation experiments were conducted using MATLAB/Simulink to verify the feasibility of the hydrogen fuel cell grid connection using the improved fractional-order sliding mode control scheme.

articleTitle: Joint Estimation of SOC and SOE for Energy Storage Lithium-ion Batteries Based on KNN Algorithm
abstract: In the battery management system, State of Charge (SOC) and State of Energy (SOE) are important parameters to guarantee the safe, reliable and efficient operation of lithium-ion batteries, and their accurate estimation plays a decisive role in the stable operation of the whole battery system. In practice, complex and variable conditions significantly affect battery characteristics and the accuracy of the state of charge (SOC) and state of energy (SOE), so accurate estimation of SOC and SOE is critical. To solve this problem, a joint SOC-SOE estimation method based on KNN algorithm is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the strong correlation correspondence between SOC-SOE was explored using the KNN algorithm. Secondly, the search method is used to determine the optimal hyperparameter values of the KNN, and finally the SOE values are corrected by combining the maximum energy obtained from the extended Kalman filtering algorithm. The experimental results show that the method can accurately estimate the SOE value with strong robustness.

articleTitle: Stability Comparison and Analysis of the VSG Controlled under Different Coordinate Systems
abstract: It has been revealed that the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) shows good stability performance in weak grid and may suffer from oscillations in strong grid. When connected to the three-phase power grid system, grid-connected voltages and currents of the VSG are usually controlled under dq coordinate system or $\alpha \beta$ coordinate system, which coordinate system is better for the VSG to avoid oscillations in strong grid is still unclear. To address that issue, this paper carries out the stability comparison and analysis of the VSG controlled under dq and $\alpha \beta$ coordinate system, respectively. Sequence-impedance models are built and validated for the VSG controlled under different coordinate systems, based on which stability comparison are carried out and key control parameters that influence the stability are figured out. It is revealed that the VSG controlled under dq coordinate system shows better stability in strong grid than the VSG controlled under $\alpha \boldsymbol{\beta}$ coordinate system. Additionally, the voltage and current control parameters have different influences on low-frequency stability of the VSG controlled under different coordinate systems in strong grid. The theoretical conclusions are also verified via simulations.

articleTitle: BatteryGPT: Battery Anomaly Detection Based on Multimodal Large Language Model
abstract: In the context of pursuing carbon neutrality goals, the importance of battery energy storage systems is becoming increasingly prominent. Battery defect detection has become critical to ensuring the safety and enhancing the efficiency of these storage systems. Current detection methods face challenges such as limited sample availability, insufficient recognition accuracy, low sensitivity to defect details, and a lack of domain-specific knowledge. To address these issues, this paper proposes a lithium-ion battery defect detection technology based on the multimodal large language model, BatteryGPT. BatteryGPT integrates a pre-trained image encoder, a multimodal text encoder, and a large language model, utilizing simulated anomaly data to locate and describe anomalies in battery images while supporting multi-turn conversations. By aligning the features of the visual and text encoders, the system derives localization results and fine-tunes the input encoding of the large language model. This approach enables the detection of unseen anomalies in batteries with only a small number of normal samples. BatteryGPT offers a more efficient solution for battery anomaly detection, with the potential to further improve the research and production efficiency of electrochemical energy storage systems.

articleTitle: A Two-Layer Optimization Strategy for Multi-Energy Microgrid in Green Power-Based Ammonia Synthesis
abstract: Driven by China's “dual carbon” policy, microgrid technology has developed rapidly. Promoting the consumption of renewable energy in microgrids is gradually attracting widespread attention. This paper studies the optimization and dispatching of microgrids coupled with wind energy, photothermal power generation, electricity to ammonia and energy storage systems. By optimizing the energy storage capacity configuration, the economic benefits and operating efficiency of the system are improved. The study adopts a two-layer optimization model. The upper layer maximizes economic benefits by reducing the investment and operating costs of the microgrid, while the lower layer focuses on the coordinated operation of the system. This article compares three scenarios. The results show that the introduction of electro-amination technology and modified particle swarm optimization algorithm (MPSO) can significantly reduce system costs, reduce wind and light abandonment and improve the economic benefits of ammonia, ultimately achieving the optimal microgrid Economical and sustainable.

articleTitle: Economic Optimization Research of Hourly-Level Intelligent Charging Stations Based on PV-Storage Charging Microgrid
abstract: With the continuous development of clean energy technologies, the PV-storage charging microgrid has become an emerging application model for electric vehicle charging stations. This paper develops an hourly-level economic optimization model based on photovoltaic generation, energy storage systems, and electric vehicle charging demand. First, the Random Forest algorithm is used to predict the photovoltaic power generation for the next 24 hours, and the Transformer model is employed to forecast the charging load of electric vehicles. Based on these predictions, an energy storage scheduling strategy is designed, and the SLSQP algorithm is used to solve the model to maximize the total revenue of the charging station. Meanwhile, system constraints, such as storage capacity limits and charge-discharge rate limits, are considered. Finally, the proposed strategy is validated with a case study of a charging station in Wuhan. Simulation results show that the optimized scheduling strategy effectively improves photovoltaic utilization, reduces the operational cost of the charging station, and enhances the overall economic efficiency of the system.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic-Storage-Charging-Swapping Model of the Electric Ship in the Inland River Port Based on Multi-energy Flow Integrated System
abstract: In order to facilitate the further expansion of electric ships, the advancement of electric ship technology must develop strategies for the rational utilization of the power grid in inland river port area. A port multi-energy integrated energy system (PMIES) model focusing on electricity flow is proposed in the paper to create a photovoltaic-storage-charging-swapping port for electric ships in the port area. The model incorporates photovoltaic (PV) and mechanical feedback energy for ship charging and swapping. The objective function is determined based on the economy expenditure of the electricity. The energy demand is evaluated under three scenarios. Lastly, the giving example illustrates how a component of the containerized battery (CB) can act as a storage device or so called “shared charger” for port energy system, with the model’s ability to lower peak demand on the grid in the port area by smoothing out fluctuations. This results in an enhanced energy efficiency for the port area while minimizing carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Joint Planning of Flexible Distribution Network Considering N-1 Criterion and Disaster Scenarios
abstract: To explore the difference between branch $\mathrm{N}-1$ criterion and resilience improvement in distributed resource planning of distribution network, a joint planning scheme for distributed resources considering both $\mathbf{N}-1$ criterion constraints and disaster scenarios is proposed. Firstly, considering normal operation scenarios, $\mathbf{N}-1$ branch faults scenarios and disaster scenarios, a mixed integer linear programming model for distribution network operation was established using stochastic programming based on the optimal power flow model. Then, in order to solve the huge computational burden brought by $\mathbf{N}-1$ scenarios, the column generation algorithm was used to split the original problem into main problem and subproblem and reduce the computational burden by iteration. The accuracy of the algorithm was guaranteed through a secondary verification. Finally, simulation experiments were conducted using IEEE33 bus system and load curtailment analysis was carried out. The experimental results show that while the substation operates normally, the distribution network planning considering branch $\mathbf{N}-1$ criterion still has good resilience in disaster scenarios with multiple branch failures.

articleTitle: Transmission network chain fault path based on coupling of typhoon disturbance and line vulnerability
abstract: The chain failure analysis of power transmission networks under the combined influence of typhoon disturbances and the vulnerability effects of transmission lines was examined. Typhoons serve as the external cause triggering natural disasters, while the line’s vulnerability effects and domino-like cascading failures represent the internal causes. Initially, the study investigates the mechanism by which the changing wind direction and velocity of typhoons induce oscillations in transmission towers and lines, leading to disasters such as tower swaying and conductor galloping. Additionally, the research explores the internal mechanisms of transmission lines and equipment facilities in service, focusing on the degradation of material mechanical properties under frequent multi-frequency and multi-amplitude external force loads and the weakening of equipment reliability due to climatic conditions over time. The combined impact of these dual causes on system failure rates and safe overload capacities is analyzed. Subsequently, the Batts typhoon wind field model and the transmission tower and line vulnerability model are established. By integrating the probability indicators of line failures caused by the dynamic path of typhoons and the correlation indicators of power flow fluctuations obtained from AC power flow analysis, the model identifies the next-level failure elements. A multi-temporal dimension failure evolution model is constructed, linking the time dimension of typhoon action with the time dimension of transmission line vulnerability effects. Finally, the proposed algorithm is analyzed and verified using the IEEE 39-node system case study and the “623 Tornado” accident in Yancheng, Jiangsu. The analysis demonstrates a strong correlation between the cascading failure paths of the power transmission network and the dynamic path of severe typhoons, validating the effectiveness and acceleration of the proposed method. This translation aims to maintain the original meaning while elevating the language to a more academic and refined level.

articleTitle: RUL and SOH Prediction for Li-ion Batteries With a Hybrid Model Using Multi-source Feature Selection and Mixed Quadratic Modal Decomposition-DBN
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) encounter multiple challenges, including difficulty in online monitoring of internal parameters and intricate capacity degradation mechanisms. Therefore, accurately predicting the state of health (SOH) and remaining useful life (RUL) of LIBs can reduce the risk of battery failure, extend their cycle life, and enable data-driven prognostics and health management (PHM). This study proposes a hybrid collaborative prediction model based on multi-source feature selection and mixed quadratic modal decomposition-deep belief network (DBN). Specifically, the indirect health indicators (IHIs) of LIBs are extracted from the constant current (CC), constant voltage (CV), impedance cycle curves, and their latent information. The multi-source feature selection is conducted on 20 different types of IHIs using Pearson and Kendall correlation analyses. To characterize capacity degradation and nonstationarity, a mixed quadratic modal decomposition model is developed. This model employs multivariate variational mode decomposition (MVMD) and improved complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (ICEEMDAN) for the optimal IHIs. Finally, a DBN model is employed to perform collaborative indirect prediction of the SOH and RUL for batteries B5, B6, B7, and B18. Experimental results indicate that the proposed model has a good predictive accuracy and generalization ability, effectively predicting the RUL and SOH of LIBs.

articleTitle: Rapid evaluation method for the carrying capacity of 5G base station load scale connected to the distribution network
abstract: With the continuous promotion of “new infrastructure”, high-density and high-energy consumption loads represented by 5 G base stations are being connected to urban distribution networks on a large scale, which has a significant impact on the safety and economic operation of the distribution network. This article proposes a fast evaluation method for the carrying capacity of 5G base station load scale connected to the distribution network based on a data-driven fast power flow calculation model. Firstly, the power consumption of 5G base stations was modeled; Secondly, a stack denoising autoencoder model is adopted to achieve fast power flow calculation in the distribution network; Then, based on the results of power flow analysis, a multi-dimensional and multi-level evaluation system for the carrying capacity of the distribution network was designed, and a quantitative score for the carrying capacity of the distribution network was given; Finally, the IEEE119 node simulation testing system was selected, and a simulation analysis of the 5G base station load scale access scenario was conducted in conjunction with the distribution network grid distribution in a certain region. Simulation shows that during peak periods of 5G base station communication tasks, when the voltage at the end nodes of distribution network branches exceeds the limit, the overall carrying capacity of the distribution network shows a downward trend. The simulation also verified that the method proposed in this article can effectively and quickly evaluate and provide the carrying capacity of urban distribution networks.

articleTitle: Optimization of The Regional Power Balance Method through Flexible Resource Cooperative Distribution Network
abstract: Under the background of new power system construction, the large number of new energy and flexible load access leads to the continuous differentiation of distribution network morphology. Power balance is becoming increasingly difficult. This paper proposes a partition balance method of distribution network based on flexible resource collaborative optimization. A balance system combining the whole network and partition balance of distribution network is established. Through the collaborative optimization of flexible resources such as energy storage and demand side response, the partition power balance is realized. Firstly, typical load scenarios are extracted based on the improved K-means algorithm. Secondly, a bi-level optimization model of partition power balance is constructed. The upper model achieves the optimal revenue of regional operators by optimizing the time-of-use electricity price, and the lower model promotes the local consumption of new energy by optimizing the energy storage capacity. The demand response and energy storage coordination optimization are used to improve the power balance ability of the distribution network, so as to improve the power balance ability of the whole network. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified based on an example of distribution network.

articleTitle: Research on Risk Analysis and Emergency Response Methods of Power Grid Operation in Cities
abstract: As power demand continues to rise and extreme weather events become more frequent, the risks confronting power grids are increasingly complex. This paper analyzes the primary risks faced by prefecture-level power grids, including equipment failures, maintenance periods, and power guarantee periods, drawing on fundamental operational conditions and risk assessment theories. Utilizing the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and fuzzy evaluation methods, we quantify the risk levels associated with the prefecture-level power grid. Comprehensive emergency countermeasures and disposal plans are proposed, with their effectiveness validated through case studies. The research findings indicate that optimized emergency plans can significantly enhance the risk resilience of prefecture-level power grids, thereby ensuring the safety and stability of power supply.

articleTitle: An Operational Risks Assessment Method for Urban AC/DC Hybrid Distribution Networks Considering Multiple Operation Uncertainties
abstract: With the swift advancement of urbanization and the growing incorporation of renewable energy sources (RES), urban power distribution systems (PDN) are evolving towards more complex AC/DC hybrid structures. These networks face multiple operational uncertainties, including fluctuating renewable generation, varying load demands, and random equipment failures, which introduce significant operational risks. This paper proposes a novel method for assessing operational risks in urban AC/DC hybrid distribution networks, considering these multiple uncertainties. The method generates typical uncertainty scenarios, evaluates system performance under these conditions, and quantifies key operational risk metrics such as renewable energy curtailment, voltage deviation, and load shedding risks. A case study using a hybrid AC/DC distribution test system demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in identifying and quantifying operational risks.

articleTitle: Surface Segmentation of 3D Point Clouds of Electrical Components Based on Gaussian Mapping
abstract: In the electrical industry, precise segmentation of 3D point cloud data is crucial for accurate geometric measurement, automated modeling, and defect detection in electrical components. However, existing segmentation methods often struggle to capture sharp features and complex details, limiting reconstruction accuracy. This paper proposes a sharp feature point detection and secondary surface segmentation method based on Gaussian mapping. The method includes three steps: identifying and correcting sharp feature point normal vectors using Gaussian mapping, performing initial segmentation, and applying a secondary fine segmentation in Euclidean space to separate surfaces with similar normal vector orientations. Experimental results on point clouds of 14 electrical components demonstrate that, compared to RG, RANSAC, RSPD, and C2NO, the proposed approach accurately detects sharp feature points and improves surface extraction accuracy.

articleTitle: Study on the factors influencing the ice shedding jump response of transmission lines
abstract: This study delves into the vibrational response triggered by the sudden detachment of ice from transmission lines, aiming for a comprehensive understanding of the factors influencing ice shedding vibration. It undertakes a thorough examination of ice shedding on transmission lines using electromagnets to mimic the weight of ice, in conjunction with off-delay time relays, to construct 16 parallel circuits. By conducting a model test, the study investigates the jumping height and dynamic tension in transmission lines under varying ice thicknesses. To broaden the scope of inquiry, a finite element analysis is performed on multi-span transmission line shedding, employing the birth and death element method. This analysis explores the effects of span length, temperature, height variations, and conductor type on the shedding response. The results indicate that simulating ice shedding using the birth and death element method yields high accuracy, with an error margin of less than 5%. Notably, the height of ice shedding jump increases with thicker ice, longer spans, and higher temperatures, while it decreases with greater height differences and smaller conductor cross-sectional areas. Similarly, the dynamic stress in transmission lines rises with thicker ice, longer spans, and greater height differences, but decreases with higher temperatures and conductor cross-sectional areas. Among these factors, ice thickness, span length, and conductor cross-sectional area have the most pronounced impact on the ice shedding response.

articleTitle: Research on Reactive Power Optimization for Port Area Grid Considering Charging Load of Electric Ships and Renewable Energy Generation
abstract: This paper focuses on the stability and economic operation challenges faced by the port power grid after integrating distributed renewable energy and shore power systems, and conducts research on reactive power distribution optimization. First, analyzing and modelling for the various source load characteristics within the power grid in the port area are carried out. The charging load characteristics of electric ships and the operation strategy of energy storage power stations are provided too. On basis of this foundation, the traditional mayfly optimization algorithm is improved by incorporating chaotic mapping and nonlinear weights, thereby enhancing the algorithm’s global search capability and convergence speed to better tackle complex reactive power optimization problems. Additionally, an optimization model for reactive power allocation in port area grids is established, with its objective function defined. Finally, through case studies, the feasibility and effectiveness of the improved algorithm are verified. The results indicate that the presented method can optimize reactive power at grid nodes, reduce system losses, and improve overall voltage stability.

articleTitle: A Knowledge Graph-based Reliability Assessment Method for Overhead Distribution Lines
abstract: Overhead distribution lines are the key to safe and reliable power supply due to their large scale, wide distribution, various types and complex operating environment. Aiming at the problems of complex data analysis and difficult reliability assessment of overhead distribution line operation and maintenance text, this paper makes full use of multi-source heterogeneous data such as line operation and maintenance logs and equipment ledger to construct overhead distribution line knowledge graph. Based on the fault mechanism and correlation analysis of individual line equipment, the equipment time-varying failure rate model and the overall reliability evaluation model of overhead distribution line based on dynamic Bayesian network are constructed. Firstly, according to the different structural characteristics of multi-source heterogeneous data, data association rules are established to construct the pattern layer, and then entities are extracted from the text data to construct the data layer to form the overhead distribution line knowledge graph. Secondly, based on the knowledge graph, repetitive power failure factors are analyzed, and the correction coefficients and weights of major power failure factors are calculated, and the real-time failure rate model of overhead distribution equipment is constructed. On this basis, the dynamic Bayesian network model is used to establish the overall reliability evaluation model of overhead distribution lines, and simulate the fault evolution process of multi-state equipment. Finally, an example is given based on the actual data of a county distribution network in Zhejiang Province. The results show that the proposed method can effectively evaluate the operational reliability of overhead distribution lines, improve the level of digital operation and maintenance management of overhead distribution lines, and ensure the safe and stable operation of power grids.

articleTitle: Optimal allocation of energy storage in distribution networks for suppressing the impactivity of high-power loads
abstract: With the increasing number of shock loads such as high-power motors in industrial parks in distribution networks, shock loads cause power quality degradation in distribution networks when they are connected and withdrawn, and energy storage is an effective method to solve the voltage quality problem. A distributed energy storage configuration method to suppress the impact of shock loads is proposed to address the voltage quality problem of distribution networks caused by shock loads. First, the impact of shock load on distribution network voltage quality is analyzed, and the boundary conditions for energy storage capacity and maximum power setting are obtained based on the analysis of the compensation mechanism of energy storage on voltage; second, a two-layer planning model for user-side energy storage configuration is established based on the boundary conditions for energy storage capacity and power, and the planning layer model optimizes the power and capacity of energy storage with the objective of minimizing the annual cost, and the operation layer model optimizes the scheduling of energy storage with the objective of minimizing the annual operation cost of the distribution network. The planning layer model optimizes the power and capacity of energy storage with the objective of minimizing annual cost, and the operation layer model optimizes the scheduling of energy storage with the objective of minimizing annual operation cost of the distribution network. The simulation results show that the proposed user-side energy storage allocation method can effectively suppress the voltage overrun problem caused by inrush loads, and at the same time, it has better economy.

articleTitle: Study and Evaluation of Carbon Emission Calculation Methods for Transmission Line Laying Projects
abstract: The urgency of addressing global climate change has led to a widespread agreement on the reduction of carbon emissions. In the realm of electric power infrastructure, assessing the carbon footprint of transmission line installation projects is crucial for advancing a low-carbon economy. This study explores the methodology for calculating carbon emissions in such projects and applies this method to a specific transmission and substation project for evaluation. Focusing on the transmission line installation project, this study initially gathers and synthesizes carbon emission calculation methodologies and criteria from analogous initiatives both domestically and internationally, drawing from existing research and pertinent literature. Subsequently, it delves into the primary carbon emission contributors within the transmission line installation project, encompassing equipment utilization, material manufacturing, transportation, and the construction phase. Then, the carbon emission accounting method of the transmission line laying project is proposed, and a case study of an actual transmission project is carried out to analyze and calculate the carbon emissions generated by each part of the construction, and the results of the carbon emissions of each part are compared. In conclusion, the study assesses the carbon emission figures for the transmission line installation project, suggests viable strategies for carbon and emission reduction, evaluates the practicality of the proposed calculation approach, identifies its limitations, and outlines potential directions for future enhancement. This aims to offer both practical guidance and theoretical insights, contributing to the sustainable growth of the electric power sector.

articleTitle: Accurate Prediction of Transmission Conductor Ice Cover Thickness Based on Ice Hazard Dynamics
abstract: Aiming at the problem of power grid accidents caused by ice disasters, this paper firstly analyzes the dynamic evolution process of ice glaze on transmission wires, and analyzes the influencing factors of ice glaze. The probability equation of the collision between supercooled water droplets and the cold wall of the wire is revealed, and the controlling effects of ambient temperature, air moisture content, wind speed, wind direction, rain and fog diameter and water film on the ice coating process of the wire are analyzed. The fluid mechanics software Fluent was used to conduct numerical simulation of the icing process of the conductor, and the influencing process of various influencing factors on the icing growth of the conductor was obtained. The wind speed and the diameter of supercooled water droplets were positively correlated with the collision coefficient, while the diameter of the conductor was negatively correlated with the collision coefficient, and the influence of various key factors on the amount of icing was studied. Based on the monitoring data of 500 kV line ice covering in Shengzhou City during the Southern ice disaster in January 2024, the ice covering thickness of transmission wires is predicted and verified with an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 2. 2 \%}$. The research results of this project can be applied in the actual ice-covering forecast, and will provide theoretical basis for China’s power grid ice-covering forecast.

articleTitle: Current Stress Optimization Control of Maximum Power Port of Triple Active Bridge Converter Based on Power Becoupling Modulation
abstract: The current optimization of triple active bridge (TAB) converter is primarily based on frequency domain models, which suffer from issues such as insufficient optimization accuracy, complex decoupling control, and a single optimization objective. To address the comprehensive requirements of optimization accuracy and multi-objective control, an optimal control method based on power decoupling modulation and time domain model is proposed, which takes the current stress of the TAB maximum power port as the optimization objective. Firstly, the TAB system with power decoupling waveform structural characteristics is equivalent to two relatively independent DABs, and the time domain modeling is carried out on this basis. Subsequently, the current stress of the maximum power port in each local optimal mode is optimized by genetic algorithm. Based on the optimization results, the intrinsic rule among the control variables within each mode are analyzed. Furthermore, corresponding optimized control variables and stress function expressions are derived based on these intrinsic rules. Finally, by comparing the current stress of different optimal operating modes, the global optimal mode and the global optimal control variables are selected. Based on the power decoupling modulation and time domain model, this method optimizes the current stress of the maximum power port of TAB, which not only realizes the power decoupling control, but also reduces the optimization complexity and enhances its accuracy. This optimal control strategy enables real-time stress optimization control under power fluctuations in the entire power range. Simulation and experiments confirm the correctness of the theoretical analysis and the effectiveness of the optimization control strategy.

Author Keywords: triple active bridge DC converter power

articleTitle: Balance Risk Assessment Method of Power System Based on CNN-BiLSTM-Attention
abstract: In view of the dual balance risks of power supply protection and consumption protection, this paper constructs the balance risk index system of power system from the two aspects of power supply protection and consumption protection. Then, on this basis, the balance risk classification standard of power system is constructed, and the balance risk levels of power system are divided. A multi-time scale evaluation method for power system balance risk based on CNN-BiLSTM-Attention is proposed. In the offline training session, the deep neural network structure was constructed based on convolutional neural network and bidirectional long short-term memory network to extract multi-spatial-temporal scale features, and the attention attention mechanism was introduced to improve the model’s ability to represent key information. In online application, transfer learning method is used to update the offline CNN-BiLSTM-Attention model under the condition of small samples in the target domain, so as to make up for the defect that the risk data characteristics cannot be well captured due to the lack of samples. Thus, the evaluation accuracy and efficiency of CNN-BiLSTM-Attention model under the new operation point can be effectively improved to realize the rapid and efficient evaluation of power system balance risk. Experiments are carried out on IEEE 30-nodes systems to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Optimization Scheduling Strategy for Microgrids with Orderly EV Charging Based on Information-Gap Decision Theory
abstract: As renewable energy rapidly develops, microgrids have gradually become an essential part of modern power systems. Microgrids integrate distributed generation, energy storage systems, and loads, improving energy utilization efficiency and offering strong resilience against disturbances. Electric vehicles (EVs), as a form of energy storage for renewable energy, have a significant impact on the operation of microgrids through their charging behavior. Proper scheduling of EV charging can not only reduce the operating costs of the microgrid but also balance loads and enhance renewable energy absorption. However, the uncertainty in DG output poses challenges to microgrid scheduling. The Information-Gap Decision Theory (IGDT) is an approach used to solve optimization problems involving uncertainty. Compared to traditional methods for handling uncertainty, such as stochastic programming, fuzzy programming, and interval robust optimization, IGDT has the advantage of not requiring precise probability distributions or uncertainty intervals for uncertain parameters. This paper proposes an optimization scheduling strategy for microgrids with orderly charging of EVs based on IGDT, analyzing the uncertainty of DG output. First, a model of EV travel characteristics and an orderly charging scheduling model are established. Then, a robust optimization model based on IGDT is constructed. The objective is to minimize the total operating cost of the microgrid.

articleTitle: Multi-user Load Forecasting Method Based on Multi-scenario Algorithm Models
abstract: With the continuous improvement of the national electricity marketization policy, it is particularly important for the generation measurement, sales side, operation side and management side to accurately predict the electricity load curve of each user in the next day and every hour of the day. In this paper, based on the historical electricity consumption data of users, cluster analysis and variational mode algorithm are first used to carry out targeted refinement and decomposition of the electricity load data, and then combined with weather data, user characteristics, electricity consumption characteristics and other data through feature fusion and feature dimension enhancement, a neural network algorithm model under multiple scenarios is established. Finally, an efficient model screening algorithm is designed to accurately predict the user’s electricity load. The results show that using the modified Imape deviation evaluation model as the benchmark, this strategy algorithm can greatly reduce the forecast deviation rate of single user’s electricity load, and improve the accuracy of the total electricity load of single user and all users.

articleTitle: Accelerated SCUC Solution: Integrating Cutting Planes, Interior Points, and Rounding Heuristics
abstract: In this research contribution, we present a novel approach aimed at accelerating online mixed-integer optimization by leveraging heuristic ROUNDING techniques and interior point methods. The cornerstone of our method lies in the construction of a Cardinality cutting plane. This Cardinality cutting plane method effectively harnesses the solution of linear programming (LP) without incorporating the CROSSOVER procedure within the interior point method. It ingeniously forms a feasible area for the segmentation of cutting planes while meticulously configuring the relevant parameters to ensure their viability. Notably, our method seamlessly integrates into any Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP) solver. Our empirical findings decisively demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed algorithm compared to conventional direct solution methods, particularly in terms of its agility in rapidly exploring feasible regions. Additionally, our algorithm exhibits a remarkable acceleration in improving the lower bound. This enhancement significantly enhances the efficiency of solving optimization problems, offering a promising avenue for effectively addressing the complexities of energy system scheduling.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Predictive Model for Electric Vehicle’s Battery’s State of Health
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are in high demand due to environmental benefits, but conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) can degrade, posing safety risks and maintenance costs. Early prediction of battery failure using multiple parameters is crucial and requires the development of an appropriate predictive algorithm for LIB state of health (SOH). There are two main categories of methods for estimating the SOH of LIB, i.e., physicsbased models and data-driven methods. Physics-based models rely on complex mathematical equations and physical knowledge of the system’s degradation behaviors, which is troublesome. Data-driven methods do not require accurate physical modelling and instead develop their own decision criteria based on training datasets. Therefore, long-short-term memory neural network (LSTMNN) model, which is a data-driven method, is a good choice for estimation of battery SOH because of its ability to learn long-term relationships between inputs and outputs. This study proposed a LSTMNN optimized by Genetic algorithm (LSTMNNGA) to overcome the issue of poor hyperparameter selection in neural networks (NNs). The robustness of the LSTMNNGA is evaluated by comparing it with the LSTMNN and an artificial neural network (ANN) model. The proposed model outperforms the approaches mentioned in the comparative study with RMSE, MAE, and MAPE of 0.0795,0.0664, and 45.31% respectively. To address the unique behavior of the test battery compared to other batteries in the dataset, potential future work could include incorporating charger voltage and impedance data, as well as experimenting with different NN architectures.

articleTitle: Low-carbon demand response strategy of power system based on event-driven mechanism
abstract: Achieving the goal of carbon neutrality necessitates the urgent transition of the power system towards decarbonization. Most existing low-carbon optimization methods for power systems primarily consider direct decarbonization from the power source side. However, it is the demand of power consumers that is the fundamental cause of carbon emissions on the power generation side. Therefore, adopting low-carbon power consumption strategies on the demand side is also one of the key measures to reduce carbon emissions. This paper proposes a low-carbon demand response (DR) strategy based on time-of-use (TOU) electricity prices and event-driven mechanisms. The strategy uses actual carbon emissions as the trigger for events and adjusts TOU electricity prices through event-driven mechanisms to guide consumers in price responsiveness, which achieves the integration of price incentive signals and carbon signals. A case study is conducted on the IEEE 39-bus system to analyze and validate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving load characteristics and reducing carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Optimal Allocation of Shared Energy Storage Capacity Considering Source-Load Interconnection in Multiple Distribution Transformer Areas
abstract: The rapid development of the Chinese economy has result in a surge in electricity demand, imposing significant strain on the transformer planning capacity within distribution areas. The substantial integration of an increasing number of renewable energy, including photovoltaics, into the grid has introduced new challenges, potentially causing grid instability and safety concerns. To adapt flexibly to regional load demands, improve the capability of high-proportion photovoltaic integration in distribution areas, reduce the peak-to-valley difference of load in distribution areas, and promote the grid’s safe and stable operation in a scientific and economic manner, this paper proposes a method for optimizing the allocation of shared energy storage capacity by considering the source-load interconnection across multiple distribution areas. The purpose of the method is to integrate the renewable energy in the distribution areas through the allocation of shared energy storage capacity. This approach concurrently alleviates the pressure on the power supply during peak power consumption in high-loaded areas, minimizes the impact of renewable energy integration on the grid, and enhances the security and stability of the grid operation. Addresses the existing problems in the distribution areas, the method establishes a model for allocating shared storage capacity based on the load characteristics, considering the construction and operation costs of the shared storage, the revenue from interaction with distribution areas, and the revenue of participation in the peak shaving ancillary service market. The model is solved by the Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm to determine the shared energy storage capacity.The Simulation results demonstrate that this method effectively allocates shared energy storage capacity between distribution areas, achieving superior peak shaving and valley filling objectives while enhancing energy storage utilization. This, in turn, leads to cost savings and profit realization.

articleTitle: Scenario Generation Method of Annual Load Series Considering Electrification Rate and Meteorological Factors
abstract: Scenario generation of annual load series serves as an important basis for long-term power system planning. Traditional methods for load scenario generation usually disregard the influence of electrification rate and meteorological factors, making it difficult to adequately represent the future development trend of power load. Therefore, this paper proposes a new scenario generation method of annual load series. First, the annual load series is reclassified based on the monthly load characteristics including non-meteorologically sensitive load and meteorologically sensitive load. For non-meteorologically sensitive load, the scenarios of load series are generated through the construction of a joint probability model of daily load characteristic indicators and an optimization model. For meteorologically sensitive load, the total load is divided into base load and temperature-related load using the load decomposition theory. Peaks and curves of temperature-related load are modeled and then superimposed onto the base load to obtain the daily load series scenarios. The case study is conducted based on the annual load data of a provincial power grid in China which verifies the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Low Carbon Collaborative Operation for Integrated Energy Microgrid with Hydrogen Storage
abstract: In order to promote the consumption of new energy and the low-carbon economic operation in microgrid cluster, under the background of sharing economy, a low-carbon collaborative optimization operation method of microgrid with shared hydrogen energy storage (SHES) based on cooperative game is proposed to give consideration to the benefits of SHES and microgrid cluster. Firstly, a framework for energy interaction and operation of SHES and microgrid cluster is proposed. Subsequently, with the goals of maximizing the operational benefits of SHES and minimizing the operational costs of each microgrid, a cooperative game-based model for the coordinated operation of electric hydrogen energy is established. Then, considering the privacy of each subject, the ADMM algorithm is used to solve the model in a distributed manner. Finally, the numerical simulation shows that the collaborative operation of SHES and various microgrids can effectively improve the operation of various entities, promote the on-site consumption of new energy, and reduce carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Coordinated Optimization Dispatch Model of Industrial Load and Shared Energy Storage in Virtual Power Plant Clusters
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-virtual power plant dispatch model based on coordinated optimization of industrial flexible loads and shared energy storage, aiming to achieve precise scheduling of three virtual power plants through a mixed-integer programming approach. In the model, industrial flexible loads are classified into three categories: transferable, reducible, and shiftable, and are jointly optimized with the shared energy storage system to achieve peak shaving, valley filling, and cost reduction. To solve the proposed optimization model, the branch and bound method is employed to ensure global optimality of the solution. The simulation results demonstrate that the coordinated adjustment of industrial flexible loads and the efficient utilization of shared energy storage significantly enhance the peak shaving and valley filling effects of the optimized power load curve, while effectively reducing daily operating costs and dependency on the grid. This study provides a theoretical foundation for coordinated optimization among multiple virtual power plants and flexible industrial load response, offering a feasible solution for constructing an efficient and economically viable new power system.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Optimization Approach for Electric Vehicle Charging Scheduling
abstract: The fast growth of electric vehicles (EVs) has led to considerable challenges in grid stability and user charging costs due to uncoordinated charging. To tackle these challenges, this paper presents an EV charging scheduling approach grounded in a multi-objective optimization framework, which integrates road network structures to enhance alignment with real-world application scenarios. First, Monte Carlo simulation is employed to model the distribution of energy demands at various nodes in the road network, revealing the potential impact of uncoordinated charging on grid load. Then, an enhanced Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization technique is proposed, featuring dynamic adjustment of inertia weights to enhance both global search capability and local convergence performance. Finally, the proposed approach is used to solve the scheduling problem, aiming to minimize the grid peak-to-average ratio and electricity costs. Numerical simulations and case studies demonstrate that this method effectively reduces charging costs, balances grid load, improves charging efficiency, and increases user satisfaction.

articleTitle: Forecast of Commercial Building Load Based on RF-CBR
abstract: The load forecast of commercial buildings is very important for power dispatching and building energy management, which can reduce building energy consumption. This paper proposes that importance scores of features can be obtained based on the Random Forest (RF) algorithm in the training process, which can be used as an important basis for the selection of feature variables. Case Based Reasoning (CBR) can make reasoning judgment on emerging cases based on existing cases and get the solutions of new cases. In this paper, the features for predicting the energy load of the target building are selected based on RF for case-based reasoning modeling, and the score of features importance for variables is used as the weight of the similarity calculation in the case-based reasoning process. The experimental results show that the modeling target can be achieved.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling Strategy of Virtual Power Plant Based on Bi-level Master-Slave Game
abstract: At present, distributed renewable energy and flexible resources such as energy storage and demand response are rapidly developing. Virtual power plants efficiently integrate distributed resources through control technology, which can improve the efficiency of distributed energy generation. Virtual power plants in the electricity market belong to various investors, forming a multi-party game pattern in the market. According to investors’ investment preferences, virtual power plants will be composed of resources with different flexibility. The article constructs a dual level master-slave game model between operators and multiple virtual power plants to balance the interests of multiple parties. Considering the mutual influence between upper level pricing and lower level output, this paper studies the dynamic price setting of operators and the optimization operation scheduling problem of virtual power plants. The lower level establish a multi virtual power plant optimization scheduling model, which aims to minimize the operating costs of each virtual power plant. The upper level aims to maximize the profit of the operator and dynamically formulate the purchase and sale price of virtual power plants based on the lower level output plan. It has been verified that the model can balance the interests of multiple parties while effectively improving the revenue of operators and reducing the operating costs of virtual power plants.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization of Energy Storage Configuration With Reliability Constraints
abstract: Aiming at the serious challenge of power system reliability, an optimal load-cutting model is established which takes into account the regulation of short-term discharge of energy storage. Energy storage can provide power support for the system for a short time, but its output is limited by capacity and upper limit. It is difficult to express the relationship between it and load reduction. To quantify the reliability improvement level of energy storage configuration, the sensitivity between the two is expanded into equality and inequality constraint sensitivity, and the state variable is taken as the intermediate variable. Finally, the sensitivity of expected demand not supplied to energy storage capacity and output upper limit is proposed. To balance the construction cost and reliability requirements of energy storage, an energy storage configuration optimization model with reliability constraints is proposed, which simplifies the reliability constraints based on the sensitivity results and avoids repeated calculations. The simulation results verify the correctness of the analytical expression of sensitivity, and the proposed optimization model can be used to guide the rational allocation of energy storage power stations and improve the reliability of the power system.

articleTitle: Research on YOLOv8 identification method of grid insulator defects caused by natural disasters
abstract: Insulators in the power system are easily aged and damaged when exposed to harsh environments for a long time, which may lead to power transmission system failures. Regular inspection is crucial to the stable operation of the system. Traditional manual inspection has low efficiency and high security risk. With the development of UAV technology, inspection based on UAV aerial images has gradually become the mainstream. However, due to the small insulator defect target and complex background, traditional image processing is difficult to meet the needs.
