Therefore, this paper proposes an insulator defect detection method based on YOLOv8 model, which realizes efficient detection under complex background through deep learning model. The open source data set and data enhancement technology are used to build high-quality data sets. Experimental results show that the recall rate of this method is 97.56% and mAP@0.5 98.86%, which has strong generalization ability and robustness. It provides an intelligent solution for power inspection and has important application value.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement and Sizing of Distributed Generation in a Distribution System Using Heap Based Optimizer
abstract: Distributed generation (DG) can help reduce the constant occurrence of power outages and voltage instability in the power system caused by an increase in load demands. This research proposes the Heap Based Optimizer (HBO), a metaheuristic optimization technique, to assess the best placements and sizes of numerous Distributed Generations (DGs) on radial distribution networks. The proposed HBO uses heap data structures and draws inspiration from organizational hierarchies. The IEEE 33-bus radial distribution network is used to verify HBO’s efficacy. The suggested HBO algorithm is contrasted with additional traditional optimization methods. The results demonstrate that HBO performed better than traditional approaches in terms of decreasing power loss, system’s voltage stability index improvement and improving the overall voltage profile.

articleTitle: Price Spread Direction Prediction Based on an Improved LSTM Model in China’s Electricity Spot Market
abstract: With the continuous development of China’s electricity spot markets, the study of bidding strategies is critical for every power generation company. This paper proposes a price spread direction prediction model based on an improved LSTM model for the electricity spot market, aiming to help power generation companies achieve higher revenues. First, we analyze the data and perform feature engineering to enrich the feature information. Second, we design the Multi-Layer LSTM model according to the data characteristics and validate it using actual data from a wind farm in Shandong Province. The results show that our model not only outperforms other models in terms of F1-Score and precision but also demonstrates higher real-world backtesting returns.

articleTitle: Long-Term Wind Power Forecasting Using Series Decomposition and Multi-Scale Attention Mechanism
abstract: With the growing global concern over carbon emissions, wind energy, as a crucial component of clean energy, plays a vital role in the power system, offering significant environmental and economic benefits. However, the intermittency and volatility of wind energy pose substantial challenges for wind power forecasting, particularly for long-term forecasting, which are essential for grid integration and system stability. Nevertheless, existing forecasting methods face challenges in addressing the complexities and nonlinear relationships inherent in wind power forecasting, such as poor model interpretability, insufficient exploration of implicit relationships between variables, and inadequate multi-scale feature capture. To tackle these issues, this paper proposes a long-term power forecasting model for wind turbines. The proposed model first decomposes the time series into trend and seasonal components. The trend component is forecasted using linear regression, while the seasonal component is forecasted by employing a two-stage attention mechanism combined with multi-scale feature extraction to explore temporal and variable-dimensional features. Finally, the two components are fused to generate a high-precision wind power forecast. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms existing state-of-the-art comparison methods in terms of forecast accuracy. On the SDWPF dataset, the model reduces the mean squared error (MSE) by an average of 8.9% and the mean absolute error (MAE) by $\mathbf{1. 7 \%}$. On the WPF dataset, the MSE decreases by $\mathbf{1 2. 6 \%}$, and the MAE decreases by $\mathbf{4. 5 \%}$. These results indicate that the proposed model offers significant advantages in long-term wind power forecasting, effectively improving prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Port-Hamiltonian System Modelling and Geometric Numerical Integrator for Synchronous Generators
abstract: Electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation is of fundamental importance for the design and operation of modern power systems. The solution of EMT models relies on numerical integration methods whose performance depends on the structure, scale, and stiffness of the system models. In this paper, we develop a synchronous generator model that maintains the underlying physical structure. In particular, a synchronous generator is represented as the interconnection of energy storage ports, dissipation ports, and external ports, leading to a canonical port-Hamiltonian system formulation. By exploiting the port-Hamiltonian structure, we introduce an energy-related invariant quantity for the developed model and construct a geometric numerical integrator based on the discrete gradient. This geometric numerical integrator can exactly maintain the energy-related invariant in the discrete-time solution. Numerical experiments verify the energy-preserving property of the proposed geometric. Comparative analysis with the Runge-Kutta method and the implicit trapezoidal method shows that, the energy-preserving geometric numerical integrator has better long-term numerical stability and accuracy especially at relatively large integration steps.

articleTitle: Intelligent Fault Diagnosis with Missing Data based on Optimization-Ensemble Learning
abstract: Fault diagnosis has become increasingly important in the operation and maintenance of modern power systems. As an essential part of daily electrical equipment, bearings have a crucial role to perform in the operation of smart grid. Currently, most of the bearing fault detection is based on relatively complete bearing datasets for diagnosis, and rarely considers the missing data type of situation. So based on the integrity considerations, this paper proposes a fault diagnosis model based on the TTAO (Triangulation topology aggregation optimizer) improved HistGradientBoostingClassifier while using the VMD-RCMFE (Refined Composite Multiscale Fuzzy Entropy) decomposition noise reduction and the feature extracted bearing dataset for random simulation of the missing data, which makes the whole study more practical significance of engineering. Following this, the different models are validated by comparison experiments using three different evaluation indexes, and the results show that the TTAO-HistGradientBoostingClassifier bearing fault classification model proposed in this paper outperforms the other models in terms of accuracy ($\mathbf{9 5. 8 2 \%}$), KAPPA coefficient (0.94), and MAF1 value (0.96), showing that it works better for missing data than the other models, showing more accurate and reliable performance for data missing class datasets.
